title.en: Volume 79: Cheng Yan, Fan Shao, Liu Taofu, Dong Shao, Feng Yuanxing, Lu Yu, Zhang Yi
title.raw: 卷79 成淹 範紹 劉桃符 劉道斌 董紹 馮元興 鹿悆 張熠 Volume 79: Cheng Yan, Fan Shao, Liu Taofu, Dong Shao, Feng Yuanxing, Lu Yu, Zhang Yi

sentences.zh: 成淹 范紹 劉桃符 劉道斌 董紹 馮元興 鹿悆 張熠

translations.literal: Cheng Yan; Fan Shao; Liu Taofu; Liu Daobin; Dong Shao; Feng Yuanxing; Lu Yu; Zhang Yi
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Yan; Fan Shao; Liu Taofu; Liu Daobin; Dong Shao; Feng Yuanxing; Lu Yu; Zhang Yi

sentences.zh: 成淹，字季文，上谷居庸人也。

translations.literal: Cheng Yan, whose courtesy name was Jiwen, was a native of Juyong in Shanggu.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Yan, courtesy name Jiwen, came from Juyong in Shanggu commandery.

sentences.zh: 自言晉侍中粲之六世孫。

translations.literal: He claimed to be a sixth-generation descendant of Cai, Palace Attendant of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: He claimed descent in the sixth generation from Cai, who had served Jin as Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 祖昇，家於北海。

translations.literal: His grandfather Sheng made his home in Beihai.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Sheng had settled the family in Beihai.

sentences.zh: 父洪，名犯顯祖廟諱，仕劉義隆，為撫軍府中兵參軍。

translations.literal: His father Hong—whose given name violated a taboo of Emperor Xianzu's temple name—served Liu Yilong as a middle army staff officer in the Pacification Army headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: His father Hong—his personal name tabooed that of Emperor Xianzu—served under Liu Yilong as a staff officer in the Pacification Army headquarters.

sentences.zh: 早卒。

translations.literal: He died young.
translations.idiomatic: He died while still young.

sentences.zh: 淹好文學，有氣尚。

translations.literal: Yan loved literature and possessed a lofty spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was devoted to letters and carried himself with spirited resolve.

sentences.zh: 劉子業輔國府刑獄參軍事，劉彧以為員外郎，假龍驤將軍，領軍主，令援東陽、歷城。

translations.literal: Under Liu Ziye he was an aide in criminal matters in the Support-the-State headquarters; Liu Yu made him an outside-section gentleman, acting Dragon-Prancing General, and army commander, ordering him to relieve Dongyang and Licheng.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Qianfei he served in the Support-the-State headquarters as an aide on penal affairs; Emperor Ming of Song appointed him an outside-section gentleman with the acting rank of Dragon-Prancing General and made him an army commander charged with relieving Dongyang and Licheng.

sentences.zh: 皇興中，降慕容白曜，赴闕，授兼著作郎。

translations.literal: In the Huangxing era he surrendered to Murong Baiyao, went to court, and was appointed acting Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In the Huangxing era he defected to Murong Baiyao, presented himself at court, and received the post of acting Compiler in the Historiography Office.

sentences.zh: 時顯祖於仲冬之月，欲巡漠北，朝臣以寒甚，固諫，並不納。

translations.literal: At that time, in the mid-winter month, Emperor Xianzu wished to tour the northern desert; the court ministers remonstrated firmly on account of the severe cold, but he accepted none of it.
translations.idiomatic: At that time, in deep winter, Emperor Xianzu planned a tour of the northern steppe; his ministers urged him to reconsider because of the bitter cold, but he would not listen.

sentences.zh: 淹上接輿釋遊論，顯祖覽之，詔尚書李訢曰：「卿等諸人不如成淹論，通釋人意。

translations.literal: Yan submitted Jieyu's essay On Loosening the Travels; when Emperor Xianzu read it, he issued an edict to Minister of the Secretariat Li Xin, saying: "You all are not the equal of Cheng Yan's essay—it truly explains what I mean.
translations.idiomatic: Yan presented his essay "On Loosening the Travels" in the manner of Jieyu; when Emperor Xianzu read it, he told Minister of the Secretariat Li Xin: "None of you understands my intent as well as Cheng Yan's piece does.

sentences.zh: 」乃敕停行。

translations.literal: " He then ordered the journey halted.
translations.idiomatic: " With that he cancelled the planned tour.

sentences.zh: 太和中，文明太后崩，蕭頤遣其散騎常侍裴昭明、散騎侍郎謝竣等來弔，欲以朝服行事。

translations.literal: In the Taihe era, after Empress Dowager Wenming died, Xiao Yi sent his Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry Pei Zhaoming, Gentleman of the Scattered Cavalry Xie Jun, and others to offer condolences, wishing to perform the rites in court dress.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taihe reign, after Empress Dowager Wenming's death, Emperor Wu of Qi sent Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry Pei Zhaoming, Gentleman of the Scattered Cavalry Xie Jun, and others to mourn, intending to conduct the condolence rites in their court robes.

sentences.zh: 主客執之，云：「弔有常式，何得以朱衣入山庭！

translations.literal: The host commissioner held to his position, saying: "Condolence rites have fixed forms—how can you enter the mourning hall in vermilion robes!
translations.idiomatic: The host commissioner stood firm, saying: "Mourning has its prescribed forms—how can you enter the mourning precinct in bright court dress!

sentences.zh: 」[1]昭明等言：「本奉朝命，不容改易。

translations.literal: " Zhaoming and the others said: "We were sent under court orders and cannot change them.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhaoming and his party replied: "We came under imperial orders and are not free to alter our dress.

sentences.zh: 」如此者數四，執志不移。

translations.literal: " This went back and forth four times, yet their resolve did not waver.
translations.idiomatic: " They argued thus four times over, and still would not yield.

sentences.zh: 高祖敕尚書李沖，令選一學識者更與論執，沖奏遣淹。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu ordered Minister of the Secretariat Li Chong to select a learned man to debate the matter further; Chong memorialized that Yan be sent.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu instructed Minister of the Secretariat Li Chong to choose a learned official to argue the point again; Chong recommended Yan and had him sent.

sentences.zh: 昭明言：「未解魏朝不聽朝服行禮，義出何典？

translations.literal: Zhaoming said: "I do not understand why the Wei court will not allow condolence in court dress—what classic authorizes this?
translations.idiomatic: Zhaoming said: "I fail to see on what authority the Wei court refuses court dress at a condolence visit—what text is this based on?

sentences.zh: 」淹言：「吉凶不同，禮有成數，玄冠不弔，童孺共聞。

translations.literal: " Yan said: "Auspice and misfortune differ, and rites have their fixed measures—one does not offer condolences in a black cap; even children have heard this.
translations.idiomatic: " Yan replied: "Joy and mourning are not the same, and ritual has its settled rules—mourning dress is not worn for a condolence call; even children know that much.

sentences.zh: 昔季孫將行，請遭喪之禮，千載之下，猶共稱之。

translations.literal: In old times, when Ji Sun was about to set out, he asked for the rites to be observed upon encountering mourning, and a thousand years later men still praise him for it.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago, when Ji Sun was about to travel, he asked what rites to follow on meeting a bereavement—and men still praise him for it a millennium later.

sentences.zh: 卿遠自江南奉慰，不能式遵成事，方謂議出何典，行人得失，何其異哉！

translations.literal: You have come from far in the south to offer condolences, yet you cannot model yourselves on established practice—and now you ask what classic our argument comes from! How strange the conduct of envoys can be!
translations.idiomatic: You have traveled from the far south to offer condolences, yet you refuse to follow established precedent—and then you ask what text our position comes from! How extraordinary the conduct of envoys can be!

sentences.zh: 」昭明言：「二國交和既久，南北皆須準望。

translations.literal: " Zhaoming said: "Our two states have been at peace for long; north and south must both take each other as standards.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhaoming said: "Our two realms have been at peace for years; north and south must hold each other to the same standard.

sentences.zh: 齊高帝崩，魏遣李彪通弔，於時初不素服，齊朝亦不以為疑，那得苦見要逼。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gao of Qi died, Wei sent Li Biao on a general condolence mission; at the time he was not in plain mourning dress at first, yet the Qi court raised no objection—why must you press us so hard now?
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gao of Qi died, Wei sent Li Biao on a condolence mission; he was not in plain mourning dress at the outset, yet the Qi court did not object—why must you press us so relentlessly now?

sentences.zh: 」淹言：「彪通弔之日，朝命以弔服自隨，而彼不遵高宗追遠之慕，乃踰月即吉，彪行弔之時，齊之君臣皆已鳴玉盈庭，貂璫曜日，百僚內外，朱服煥然，彪行人不被主人之命，復何容獨以素服間衣冠之中？

translations.literal: " Yan said: "On the day of Biao's general condolence mission, the court had ordered mourning garments brought along, but Qi did not observe the longing of High Ancestor for his forebears and returned to auspicious dress after only a month had passed. When Biao went to offer condolences, the rulers and ministers of Qi were already jade-clad and filling the hall, their sable and rank insignia dazzling in the sun; inside and outside, the hundred officials shone in vermilion robes. Biao's envoys had received no command from their hosts—how could they alone have worn plain dress amid such court regalia?
translations.idiomatic: " Yan replied: "When Biao went on his condolence mission, the Wei court had ordered mourning dress brought along, but Qi failed to honor the filial mourning of High Ancestor and returned to normal dress after only a month. By the time Biao arrived, Qi's rulers and ministers were already arrayed in full court splendor—jade pendants chiming, rank badges gleaming, officials inside and out in bright robes. Biao's party had received no permission from their hosts—how could they alone have worn plain mourning amid such finery?

sentences.zh: 來責雖高，未敢聞命。

translations.literal: Your rebuke is weighty, yet I dare not accept your command.
translations.idiomatic: Your reproach carries weight, but I cannot accept your demand.

sentences.zh: 我皇帝仁孝之性，侔於有虞，處諒闇以來，百官聽於冢宰，卿豈得以此方彼也。

translations.literal: Our emperor's nature in benevolence and filial piety equals that of Yu of Shun; since he entered the mourning seclusion, the hundred officials have taken their orders from the regent—how can you compare that situation with this one?
translations.idiomatic: Our emperor's filial devotion rivals that of Shun; since he entered mourning seclusion, the hundred officials have obeyed the regent—how can you equate your case with that one?

sentences.zh: 」昭明乃搖膝而言：「三皇不同禮，亦安知得失所歸。

translations.literal: " Zhaoming then swayed on his knees and said: "The Three Sovereigns did not share the same rites—who can tell where right and wrong lie?
translations.idiomatic: " Zhaoming shifted on his seat and said: "The Three Sovereigns did not follow one ritual code—who can say where right and wrong lie?

sentences.zh: 」淹言：「若如來談，卿以虞舜、高宗為非也？

translations.literal: " Yan said: "If what you say is so, you hold Shun of Yu and High Ancestor to be in the wrong?
translations.idiomatic: " Yan said: "If that is your view, you are saying Shun and High Ancestor were wrong?

sentences.zh: 」昭明遂相顧而笑曰：「非孝者，宣尼有成責，行人亦弗敢言。

translations.literal: " Zhaoming then looked at one another and laughed, saying: "Confucius has fixed rebukes for the unfilial—envoys dare not speak of such things.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhaoming exchanged glances and laughed: "Confucius left settled rebukes for the unfilial—envoys dare not speak of such matters.

sentences.zh: 希主人裁以弔服，使人唯齎袴褶，比既戎服，不可以弔，幸借緇衣㡊，以申國命。

translations.literal: We hope the host will grant mourning dress; our envoys brought only trousers and short jackets. As we are now in military dress, we cannot offer condolences—may we borrow black robes and skirts to fulfill our state's commission?
translations.idiomatic: We ask that our hosts provide mourning dress; our envoys brought only field trousers and jackets. In military dress we cannot perform the rites—may we borrow black mourning garments to carry out our state's orders?

sentences.zh: 今為魏朝所逼，違負指授，還南之日，必得罪本朝。

translations.literal: Now, pressed by the Wei court, if we violate our orders, on the day we return south we are sure to be punished by our own court.
translations.idiomatic: If the Wei court forces us to disobey our orders, we are certain to be punished at home when we return south.

sentences.zh: 」淹言：「彼有君子也，卿將命折中，還南之日，應有高賞；

translations.literal: " Yan said: "If there are worthy men in your state, you will carry out your commission with balanced judgment, and on your return south you should receive high reward;
translations.idiomatic: " Yan said: "If your court has men of integrity, you will fulfill your mission with principled compromise and should be richly rewarded when you return south;

sentences.zh: 若無君子也，但令有光國之譽，雖復非理見罪，亦復何嫌。

translations.literal: if there are no worthy men, so long as you win honor for your state, even if you are punished without reason, what is there to regret?
translations.idiomatic: if there are not, so long as you bring honor to your state, even unjust punishment is nothing to fear.

sentences.zh: 南史、董孤，自當直筆。

translations.literal: The Historian of the South and Dong Gu will surely set it down with an upright brush.
translations.idiomatic: Historians such as the Recorder of the South and Dong Gu will write the truth plainly.

sentences.zh: 」既而，高祖遣李沖問淹昭明所言，淹以狀對。

translations.literal: " Shortly afterward, Emperor Gaozu sent Li Chong to ask Yan what Zhaoming had said, and Yan reported the facts.
translations.idiomatic: " Soon after, Emperor Gaozu sent Li Chong to inquire what had passed between Yan and Zhaoming; Yan gave a full account.

sentences.zh: 高祖詔沖曰：「我所用得人。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu issued an edict to Chong: "The man I employed was the right one.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told Chong: "I chose the right man for this.

sentences.zh: 」仍敕送衣㡊給昭明等，賜淹果食。

translations.literal: " He then ordered robes and skirts sent to Zhaoming and the others, and bestowed fruit and food on Yan.
translations.idiomatic: " He then had mourning garments sent to Zhaoming's party and rewarded Yan with fruit and refreshments.

sentences.zh: 明旦引昭明等入，皆令文武盡哀。

translations.literal: The next morning he led Zhaoming and the others in, and ordered all civil and military officials to mourn fully.
translations.idiomatic: The next morning he admitted Zhaoming and his party and required the full court, civil and military alike, to observe mourning.

sentences.zh: 後正侍郎。

translations.literal: Later he was made Regular Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: He was later promoted to Regular Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 高祖以淹清貧，賜絹百匹。

translations.literal: Because Yan was poor though upright, Emperor Gaozu bestowed on him a hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: Finding Yan upright but poor, Emperor Gaozu gave him a hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 十六年，蕭賾遣其散騎常侍庾蓽、散騎侍郎何憲、主書邢宗慶朝貢，值朝廷有事明堂，因登靈臺以觀雲物。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, Xiao Ze sent his Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry Yu Bi, Gentleman of the Scattered Cavalry He Xian, and Chief Clerk Xing Zongqing on a tribute mission; the court was then occupied with the Bright Hall, and they ascended the Spirit Terrace to observe cloud signs.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year, Emperor Ming of Qi sent Regular Attendant Yu Bi, Gentleman He Xian, and Chief Clerk Xing Zongqing to present tribute; the Wei court was preparing rites at the Bright Hall, and the envoys were taken up the Spirit Terrace to observe the heavens.

sentences.zh: 高祖敕淹引蓽等館南矚望行禮，事畢，還外館，賜酒食。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu ordered Yan to lead Bi and the others to the southern lodge to watch the rites; when the ceremony was finished, they returned to the outer hostel and were given wine and food.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu had Yan escort Bi's party to the southern lodge to witness the rites; when the ceremony ended they returned to the guest quarters and were entertained with wine and food.

sentences.zh: 宗慶語淹言：「南北連和既久，而比棄信絕好，為利而動，豈是大國善隣之義？

translations.literal: Zongqing said to Yan: "North and south have long been at peace, yet lately you have cast aside faith and broken good relations, moving for profit—can this be the way a great state treats a good neighbor?
translations.idiomatic: Zongqing said to Yan: "North and south have been at peace for years, yet you have lately broken faith and ended goodwill, acting for gain alone—is this how a great power treats a neighbor?

sentences.zh: 」淹言：「夫為王者，不拘小節。

translations.literal: " Yan said: "One who would be king is not bound by minor points.
translations.idiomatic: " Yan replied: "A true sovereign does not cling to petty scruples.

sentences.zh: 中原有菽，工採者獲多，豈眷眷守尾生之信。

translations.literal: In the Central Plains there are beans—those skilled at gathering reap the most; why should one cling stubbornly to the faith of Weisheng?
translations.idiomatic: The Central Plains are rich in beans—skilled gatherers take the most; why cling stubbornly to the punctilio of Weisheng?

sentences.zh: 且齊先主歷事宋朝，荷恩積世，當應便爾欺奪？

translations.literal: Moreover, your former ruler served the Song dynasty for generations and received accumulated grace—should he so lightly have seized and robbed?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, your founding ruler served the Song house for generations and owed it deep gratitude—was he right to seize power so lightly?

sentences.zh: 」宗慶、庾蓽及行者皆相顧失色。

translations.literal: " Zongqing, Yu Bi, and all the envoys looked at one another and changed color.
translations.idiomatic: " Zongqing, Yu Bi, and the entire embassy exchanged glances and blanched.

sentences.zh: 何憲知淹昔從南入，而以手掩目曰：「卿何為不作于禁，而作魯肅？

translations.literal: He Xian, knowing Yan had once come in from the south, covered his eyes with his hand and said: "Why do you not act like Yu Jin, but instead like Lu Su?
translations.idiomatic: He Xian, knowing Yan had once defected from the south, covered his eyes and said: "Why play not Yu Jin but Lu Su?

sentences.zh: 」淹言：「我捨危効順，欲追蹤陳、韓，何于禁之有！

translations.literal: " Yan said: "I left peril to follow righteousness, wishing to follow the track of Chen and Han—what has that to do with Yu Jin!
translations.idiomatic: " Yan replied: "I left danger to serve a righteous cause, seeking to follow the example of Chen Ping and Han Xin—what has that to do with Yu Jin!

sentences.zh: 」憲亦不對。

translations.literal: " Xian made no reply.
translations.idiomatic: " Xian had no answer.

sentences.zh: 王肅歸國也，高祖以淹曾官江表，詔觀是非。

translations.literal: When Wang Su returned to the state, Emperor Gaozu, because Yan had once served south of the Yangzi, ordered him to observe whether Su was sincere or false.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Su defected to Wei, Emperor Gaozu—knowing Yan had once served south of the Yangzi—ordered him to judge Su's sincerity.

sentences.zh: 乃造肅與語，還奏言實。

translations.literal: He then went to visit Su and converse with him, and on returning memorialized that Su was genuine.
translations.idiomatic: He visited Su and spoke with him, then reported back that Su's loyalty was genuine.

sentences.zh: 時議紛紜，猶謂未審。

translations.literal: Opinion at the time was divided, and many still held that the matter was not settled.
translations.idiomatic: Court opinion was still divided, and many doubted the matter was settled.

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「明日引入，我與語，自當知之。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu said: "Tomorrow bring him in; I will speak with him myself and then I shall know.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Bring him in tomorrow; I will speak with him myself and judge.

sentences.zh: 」及鑾輿行幸，肅多扈從，敕淹將引，若有古跡，皆使知之。

translations.literal: " When the imperial carriage went on tour, Su often followed in attendance; the emperor ordered Yan to lead and guide him, and wherever there were ancient sites, he was to have Su informed of them.
translations.idiomatic: " On the imperial tour Su often rode in attendance; the emperor ordered Yan to serve as guide and point out every historic site along the way.

sentences.zh: 行到朝歌，肅問此是何城。

translations.literal: When they reached Chaoge, Su asked what city this was.
translations.idiomatic: When they came to Chaoge, Su asked what city it was.

sentences.zh: 淹言紂都朝歌城。

translations.literal: Yan said it was the capital of King Zhou, the city of Chaoge.
translations.idiomatic: Yan said it was the capital of King Zhou of Shang—Chaoge.

sentences.zh: 肅言：「故應有殷之頑民也。

translations.literal: Su said: "So there ought still to be the stubborn people of Yin here.
translations.idiomatic: Su said: "Then there should still be remnants of the stubborn people of Yin here.

sentences.zh: 」淹言：「昔武王滅紂，悉居河洛，中因劉石亂華，仍隨司馬東渡。

translations.literal: " Yan said: "In old times King Wu destroyed Zhou and settled them all in the He-Luo region; later, because of the Liu and Shi disorders in China, they followed the Sima clan east across the river.
translations.idiomatic: " Yan said: "When King Wu overthrew Zhou he resettled them all in the He-Luo region; later, during the upheavals of the Liu and Shi, they followed the Sima house east across the Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 」肅知淹寓於青州，乃笑而謂淹曰：「青州間何必無其餘種。

translations.literal: " Su, knowing Yan had once lived in Qing Province, laughed and said to Yan: "Why should there not be remnants of them in Qing Province as well?
translations.idiomatic: " Su, knowing Yan had once lived in Qing Province, laughed and said: "Why should Qing Province lack such remnants as well?

sentences.zh: 」淹以肅本隸徐州，言：「青州本非其地，徐州間今日重來，非所知也。

translations.literal: " Yan, knowing Su was originally from Xu Province, said: "Qing Province was never their territory; as for Xu Province, whether they have returned there today, I do not know.
translations.idiomatic: " Yan, knowing Su came from Xu Province, replied: "Qing was never their homeland; as for Xu, whether they have returned there today, I could not say.

sentences.zh: 」肅遂伏馬上掩口而笑，顧謂侍御史張思寧曰：「向者聊因戲言，遂致辭溺。

translations.literal: " Su then leaned on his horse, covered his mouth, and laughed, turning to Attending Censor Zhang Sining and saying: "Just now, in a bit of banter, I was drawn into an exchange of words and got the worse of it.
translations.idiomatic: " Su leaned over his saddle, covered his mouth, and laughed, then turned to Attending Censor Zhang Sining: "A moment ago, in jest, I talked myself into a verbal drowning.

sentences.zh: 」思寧馳馬奏聞，高祖大悅，謂彭城王勰曰：「淹此段足為制勝。

translations.literal: " Sining galloped ahead to report; Emperor Gaozu was greatly pleased and said to Prince Pengcheng Xie: "In this exchange Yan was fully equal to gaining the victory.
translations.idiomatic: " Sining rode ahead to report; the emperor was delighted and told Prince Pengcheng Xie: "In that exchange Yan more than held his own.

sentences.zh: 」輿駕至洛，肅因侍宴。

translations.literal: " When the imperial carriage reached Luoyang, Su attended a banquet.
translations.idiomatic: " When the court reached Luoyang, Su attended a banquet.

sentences.zh: 高祖戲肅曰：「近者行次朝歌，聞成淹共卿殊有往覆，卿試重敍之。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu jested with Su: "On the recent journey, when we stopped at Chaoge, I heard that you and Cheng Yan had quite an exchange—try telling it again.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor teased Su: "On our recent stop at Chaoge I heard you and Cheng Yan had quite a verbal duel—tell us again.

sentences.zh: 」肅言：「臣前朝歌為淹所困，不謂此事仰聞聽覽。

translations.literal: " Su said: "Your servant was once trapped by Yan at Chaoge; I did not think this matter had reached Your Majesty's ears.
translations.idiomatic: " Su said: "I was bested by Yan at Chaoge; I did not think Your Majesty had heard of it.

sentences.zh: 臣爾日失言，一之已甚，豈宜再說。

translations.literal: Your servant misspoke that day; once is already too much—how could I tell it again?
translations.idiomatic: I misspoke that day; once was already too much—how could I repeat it?

sentences.zh: 」遂皆大笑。

translations.literal: " All then burst into loud laughter.
translations.idiomatic: " Everyone laughed aloud.

sentences.zh: 高祖又謂肅曰：「淹能制卿，其才亦不困。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu also said to Su: "Yan was able to get the better of you—his talent is not slight.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor added: "Yan got the better of you—his talent is no small thing.

sentences.zh: 」肅言：「淹才詞便為難有，聖朝宜應敍進。

translations.literal: " Su said: "Yan's literary talent and eloquence are hard to match; the sacred court ought to promote him.
translations.idiomatic: " Su said: "Yan's literary gifts and eloquence are rare; the court ought to promote him.

sentences.zh: 」高祖言：「若因此進淹，恐辱卿轉甚。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "If I promote Yan on this account, I fear your disgrace will only deepen.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said: "If I promote Yan because of this, your embarrassment will only grow.

sentences.zh: 」肅言：「臣屈己達人，正可顯臣之美。

translations.literal: " Su said: "Your servant humbles himself to advance others—this only shows your servant's virtue.
translations.idiomatic: " Su said: "By yielding to advance another, I only show my own magnanimity.

sentences.zh: 」高祖曰：「卿既為人所屈，欲求屈己之名，復於卿太優。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "You were already bested by another, yet you seek the name of one who humbles himself—that is too generous toward you.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said: "You were already bested, yet you claim the credit of humility—that flatters you too much.

sentences.zh: 」肅言：「淹既蒙進，臣得屈己伸人，此所謂陛下惠而不費。

translations.literal: " Su said: "Since Yan has received promotion, your servant has been able to humble himself and raise another—this is what is called Your Majesty's bounty without cost.
translations.idiomatic: " Su said: "If Yan is promoted, I humble myself to exalt another—Your Majesty's grace at no expense to the treasury.

sentences.zh: 」遂酣笑而止。

translations.literal: " They then laughed heartily and let the matter rest.
translations.idiomatic: " With that they laughed themselves to a stop.

sentences.zh: 乃賜淹龍廐上馬一匹，并鞍勒宛具、朝服一襲，轉謁者僕射。

translations.literal: He then bestowed on Yan one superior horse from the Dragon Stable, together with saddle, bridle, and full trappings, and one set of court robes, and transferred him to be Supervisor of the Imperial Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He then gave Yan a top-grade horse from the imperial stables with full saddle and trappings, a set of court robes, and appointed him Supervisor of the Imperial Gate.

sentences.zh: 時遷都，高祖以淹家無行資，敕給事力，送至洛陽，并賜假日與家累相隨。

translations.literal: At the time of the capital transfer, because Yan's household lacked travel funds, the emperor ordered attendants provided and had them escorted to Luoyang, also granting leave so they could travel with their families.
translations.idiomatic: During the move of the capital, finding Yan's family without means to travel, the emperor assigned servants to escort them to Luoyang and granted leave so they could bring their households along.

sentences.zh: 行次靈丘，屬蕭鸞遣使，敕驛馬徵淹。

translations.literal: When they reached Lingqiu, Xiao Luan happened to send envoys; the emperor ordered relay horses to summon Yan.
translations.idiomatic: At Lingqiu, when Xiao Luan sent envoys, the emperor ordered relay horses to summon Yan at once.

sentences.zh: 車駕濟淮，淹於路左請見，高祖竚駕而進之。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage crossed the Huai, Yan requested an audience on the roadside; Emperor Gaozu halted the carriage and had him approach.
translations.idiomatic: As the imperial procession crossed the Huai, Yan requested an audience from the roadside; the emperor halted and had him brought forward.

sentences.zh: 淹曰：「蕭鸞悖虐，幽明同棄，陛下俯應人神，按劍江涘，然敵不可小，蜂蠆有毒，而況國乎？

translations.literal: Yan said: "Xiao Luan is perverse and cruel; both the living and the dead have cast him off. Your Majesty humbly responds to men and spirits and has drawn your sword at the river's edge—yet the enemy must not be slighted: even bees and scorpions have venom, how much more a state!
translations.idiomatic: Yan said: "Xiao Luan is cruel and perverse; heaven and earth alike reject him. Your Majesty answers the call of men and gods with sword drawn at the river's edge—yet the enemy must not be underestimated: even bees and scorpions have their sting, and this is a whole kingdom.

sentences.zh: 深願聖明保萬全之策。

translations.literal: I deeply hope Your Sagely Brightness will keep to a strategy of complete safety.
translations.idiomatic: I earnestly pray Your Majesty will keep to a strategy that leaves nothing to chance.

sentences.zh: 」詔曰：「此前車之轍，得不慎乎！

translations.literal: " An edict said: "The tracks of the overturned cart ahead—can one fail to be cautious!
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor replied: "The overturned cart ahead—should I not be cautious?

sentences.zh: 」淹曰：「伏聞發洛已來，諸有諫者，解官奪職，恐非聖明納下之義。

translations.literal: " Yan said: "I have heard that since leaving Luoyang, all who remonstrated have been dismissed and stripped of office— I fear this is not the way of a sage ruler in accepting counsel from below.
translations.idiomatic: " Yan said: "I have heard that since we left Luoyang, every man who remonstrated has been dismissed— I fear that is not how a sage ruler welcomes counsel from below.

sentences.zh: 」高祖曰：「此是我命耳，卿不得為干斧鉞。

translations.literal: " Emperor Gaozu said: "This is my own command— you must not interfere with the axe and halberd.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said: "That is my own decision—you must not meddle with military matters.

sentences.zh: 」淹曰：「昔文王詢於芻蕘，晉文聽輿人之誦，臣雖卑賤，敢同匹夫。

translations.literal: " Yan said: "In old times King Wen inquired of grass-cutters and firewood-gatherers, and Duke Wen of Jin listened to the songs of cart-drivers; your servant, though lowly, dares to stand with the common man.
translations.idiomatic: " Yan said: "King Wen once sought counsel from woodcutters; Duke Wen of Jin listened to songs from the roadside. Though I am humble, I dare speak as any common man may.

sentences.zh: 」高祖優而容之，詔賜絹百匹。

translations.literal: " Emperor Gaozu was gracious and indulgent toward him and issued an edict bestowing a hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor received him graciously and ordered a hundred bolts of silk bestowed on him.

sentences.zh: 高祖幸徐州，敕淹與閭龍駒等主舟檝，將汎泗入河，泝流還洛。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu visited Xuzhou, he ordered Yan and Lü Longju and others to take charge of boats and oars, intending to sail the Si into the Yellow River and return to Luoyang against the current.
translations.idiomatic: On a visit to Xuzhou, the emperor put Yan and Lü Longju in charge of the fleet, planning to sail the Si into the Yellow River and return upstream to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 軍次碻磝，淹以黃河浚急，慮有傾危，乃上疏陳諫。

translations.literal: When the army halted at Qiaolao, Yan, because the Yellow River ran swift and deep, feared capsizing and submitted a memorial of remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: When the army halted at Qiaolao, Yan, fearing the Yellow River's swift current might capsize the boats, submitted a memorial urging caution.

sentences.zh: 高祖敕淹曰：「朕以恒代無運漕之路，故京邑民貧。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu issued an edict to Yan: "I consider that Heng and Dai had no water transport route, and so the capital's people were poor.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied: "Because Heng and Dai had no canal route, the capital region was poor.

sentences.zh: 今移都伊洛，欲通運四方，而黃河急浚，人皆難涉。

translations.literal: Now, having moved the capital to Yiluo, I wish to open transport in all directions, yet the Yellow River runs swift and deep and all find it hard to cross.
translations.idiomatic: Now that we have moved the capital to the Yi-Luo region, I wish to open transport in every direction, yet the Yellow River runs swift and deep and everyone finds it hard to cross.

sentences.zh: 我因有此行，必須乘流，所以開百姓之心。

translations.literal: Because of this I must make this journey and ride the current, so as to open the hearts of the common people.
translations.idiomatic: That is why I must make this voyage and ride the current—to open the people's minds to what is possible.

sentences.zh: 知卿至誠，而今者不得相納。

translations.literal: I know your utmost sincerity, but on this occasion I cannot accept your counsel.
translations.idiomatic: I know your counsel comes from loyalty, but this time I cannot heed it.

sentences.zh: 」敕賜驊騮馬一匹，衣冠一襲。

translations.literal: " He ordered a piebald steed and one set of robes and cap bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: " He then bestowed a piebald horse and a full set of robes.

sentences.zh: 除羽林監，領主客令，加威遠將軍。

translations.literal: He was appointed Supervisor of the Feathered Forest, concurrently held the post of Director of Guests, and was given the additional rank of General Who Establishes Might from Afar.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Supervisor of the Feathered Forest, retained the post of Director of Guests, and received the additional rank of General Who Establishes Might from Afar.

sentences.zh: 于時宮殿初構，經始務廣，兵民運材，日有萬計，伊洛流澌，苦於厲涉，淹遂啟求，敕都水造浮航。

translations.literal: At that time the palaces were first under construction and the undertaking was vast; soldiers and civilians hauling materials numbered tens of thousands daily. The Yi and Luo ran with ice floes, and crossing was painfully difficult; Yan thereupon petitioned, and an edict ordered the Director of Waterways to build pontoon bridges.
translations.idiomatic: The palaces were then newly rising on a vast scale; tens of thousands of soldiers and laborers hauled materials each day. The Yi and Luo ran with ice, making crossings arduous; Yan petitioned for relief, and the emperor ordered the Director of Waterways to build pontoon bridges.

sentences.zh: 高祖賞納之，意欲榮淹於眾，朔旦受朝，百官在位，乃賜帛百匹，知左右二都水事。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu praised and accepted this; wishing to honor Yan before the assembly, on the first morning of the month when the court received audience and all officials were in place, he bestowed a hundred bolts of silk and made him overseer of both left and right Directorates of Waterways.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved and wished to honor Yan before the court; on the first day of the month, with all officials present at audience, he gave Yan a hundred bolts of silk and put him in charge of both Directorates of Waterways.

sentences.zh: 世宗初，司徒、彭城王勰曰：「先帝本有成旨，淹有歸國之誠，兼歷官著稱，宜加優陟。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Shizong's reign, the Minister of Education, Prince Pengcheng Xie, said: "The late emperor already had a settled intent; Yan showed sincere loyalty in coming to our state and has distinguished himself in successive offices—he should receive preferential promotion.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Xuanwu's reign, Prince Pengcheng Xie, Minister of Education, said: "The late emperor had already resolved to advance him; Yan showed true loyalty in defecting and has served with distinction—he deserves preferential promotion.

sentences.zh: 高祖雖崩，詔猶在耳。

translations.literal: Though Emperor Gaozu has passed away, his edict is still in our ears.
translations.idiomatic: Though Emperor Gaozu is gone, his words still ring in our ears.

sentences.zh: 」乃相聞選曹，加淹右軍，領左右都水，仍主客令。

translations.literal: " He then notified the Selection Bureau, and Yan was given the additional post of Right Army Commander, continuing to head both Directorates of Waterways while retaining the Directorship of Guests.
translations.idiomatic: " He notified the Selection Bureau, and Yan was promoted to Right Army Commander, continuing to head both Directorates of Waterways while retaining the Directorship of Guests.

sentences.zh: 復授驍騎將軍，加輔國將軍，都水、主客如故。

translations.literal: He was again given the rank of Valiant Cavalry General and the additional rank of General Who Supports the State; his posts in the Waterways and Guests offices remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was further made Valiant Cavalry General with the additional rank of General Who Supports the State; his waterways and guest-reception duties were unchanged.

sentences.zh: 淹小心畏法，典客十年，四方貢聘，皆有私遺，毫釐不納，乃至衣食不充。

translations.literal: Yan was careful and fearful of the law; for ten years as director of guests, tribute and embassies from all quarters brought him private gifts, yet he accepted not the slightest fraction, until even his food and clothing were insufficient.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was scrupulous and law-abiding; for ten years as director of guests, envoys from every quarter offered him private gifts, but he refused every fraction, until he could scarcely afford food and clothing.

sentences.zh: 遂啟乞外祿。

translations.literal: He then petitioned to request an outside salary.
translations.idiomatic: He then petitioned for an appointment outside the capital.

sentences.zh: 景明三年，出除平陽太守，將軍如故。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jingming he was sent out and appointed Administrator of Pingyang, his general's rank remaining as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jingming he was appointed Administrator of Pingyang, retaining his general's rank.

sentences.zh: 還朝，病卒。

translations.literal: On returning to court he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to court and died of illness.

sentences.zh: 贈本將軍、光州刺史，諡曰定。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given his former general's rank and made Governor of Guang Province, with the posthumous title Ding.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored with his former general's rank and the governorship of Guang Province, with the posthumous name Ding.

sentences.zh: 子霄，字景鸞。

translations.literal: His son Xiao, courtesy name Jingluan.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xiao, courtesy name Jingluan.

sentences.zh: 亦學涉，好為文詠，但詞彩不倫，率多鄙俗。

translations.literal: He too was broadly learned and loved to compose literary pieces, but his diction was undistinguished and mostly vulgar.
translations.idiomatic: He too was widely read and fond of literary composition, but his style was uneven and mostly coarse.

sentences.zh: 與河東姜質等朋遊相好，詩賦間起。

translations.literal: With Jiang Zhi of Hedong and others he formed a friendly literary circle, and poems and rhapsodies arose among them.
translations.idiomatic: He formed a literary circle with Jiang Zhi of Hedong and others, and poems and fu pieces flowed among them.

sentences.zh: 知音之士，共所嗤笑；

translations.literal: connoisseurs of literature all ridiculed them together;
translations.idiomatic: Men of taste mocked them together;

sentences.zh: 閭巷淺識，頌諷成羣，乃至大行於世。

translations.literal: yet shallow folk of the alleys praised them in crowds, until they circulated widely in the world.
translations.idiomatic: yet shallow folk in the lanes praised them in crowds, until their works spread widely.

sentences.zh: 歷治書侍御史而卒。

translations.literal: He served as Attending Censor for Legal Documents and then died.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Attending Censor for Legal Documents and died in office.

sentences.zh: 范紹，字始孫，敦煌龍勒人。

translations.literal: Fan Shao, courtesy name Shisun, was a native of Longle in Dunhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Shao, courtesy name Shisun, came from Longle in Dunhuang commandery.

sentences.zh: 少而聰敏。

translations.literal: From youth he was clever and quick.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood he was clever and quick-witted.

sentences.zh: 年十二，父命就學，師事崔光。

translations.literal: At twelve his father ordered him to pursue study, and he took Cui Guang as his teacher.
translations.idiomatic: At twelve his father sent him to study under Cui Guang.

sentences.zh: 以父憂廢業，母又誡之曰：「汝父卒日，令汝遠就崔生，希有成立。

translations.literal: Because of mourning for his father he abandoned his studies; his mother admonished him again, saying: "On the day your father died he ordered you to go far to study with Master Cui, hoping you would achieve something.
translations.idiomatic: Mourning for his father interrupted his studies; his mother admonished him: "On his deathbed your father sent you far away to study with Master Cui, hoping you would make something of yourself.

sentences.zh: 今已過期，宜遵成命。

translations.literal: The mourning period has now passed; you should follow his final command.
translations.idiomatic: The mourning period is over; you should honor his last wish.

sentences.zh: 」紹還赴學。

translations.literal: " Shao returned to resume his studies.
translations.idiomatic: " Shao returned to his studies.

sentences.zh: 太和初，充太學生，轉算生，頗涉經史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taihe he became a student of the Imperial Academy, then a calendar student, and became well versed in the classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Taihe reign he entered the Imperial Academy, then became a calendar student, and gained broad knowledge of the classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 十六年，高祖選為門下通事令史，遷錄事，令掌奏文案，高祖善之。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year Emperor Gaozu selected him as a communications clerk under the Gate, promoted him to recorder, and ordered him to manage memorials and documents; the emperor was pleased with him.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year Emperor Gaozu made him a communications clerk under the Gate, then recorder in charge of memorials and documents; the emperor was pleased with his work.

sentences.zh: 又為侍中李沖、黃門崔光所知，出內文奏，多以委之。

translations.literal: He was also recognized by Palace Attendant Li Chong and Yellow Gate Cui Guang; drafts for internal and external documents were largely entrusted to him.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Li Chong and Cui Guang of the Yellow Gate also recognized his ability; most drafts for court documents were entrusted to him.

sentences.zh: 高祖曾謂近臣曰：「崔光從容，范紹之力。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu once said to his close ministers: "Cui Guang is at ease; Fan Shao is forceful.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu once told his close ministers: "Cui Guang is unhurried; Fan Shao is forceful.

sentences.zh: 」稍遷強弩將軍、積弩將軍、公車令，加給事中，遷羽林監。

translations.literal: " He was gradually promoted to General of Strong Crossbows, General of Accumulated Crossbows, and Director of the Imperial Carriages, given the additional post of Palace Attendant, and transferred to Supervisor of the Feathered Forest.
translations.idiomatic: " He rose through the ranks to General of Strong Crossbows, General of Accumulated Crossbows, and Director of the Imperial Carriages, was made an additional Palace Attendant, and became Supervisor of the Feathered Forest.

sentences.zh: 揚州刺史、任城王澄請征鍾離，敕紹詣壽春，共量進止。

translations.literal: The Governor of Yang Province, Prince of Rencheng Yuan Cheng, requested an expedition against Zhongli; an edict ordered Shao to go to Shouchun and jointly assess whether to advance or halt.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Rencheng Yuan Cheng, governor of Yang Province, sought permission to attack Zhongli; the emperor sent Shao to Shouchun to assess the campaign with him.

sentences.zh: 澄曰：「須兵十萬，往還百日，渦陽、鍾離、廣陵、廬江，欲數道俱進，但糧仗軍資，須朝廷速遣。

translations.literal: Cheng said: "I need a hundred thousand troops, a round trip of a hundred days; Woyang, Zhongli, Guangling, and Lujiang—I wish to advance on several routes at once, but grain, weapons, and military supplies must be sent swiftly by the court.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng said: "I need a hundred thousand men and a hundred days there and back. I plan to advance on Woyang, Zhongli, Guangling, and Lujiang by several routes at once, but the court must send grain, arms, and supplies at once.

sentences.zh: 」紹曰：「計十萬之眾，往還百日，須糧百日。

translations.literal: " Shao said: "Counting a force of a hundred thousand, a round trip of a hundred days requires provisions for a hundred days.
translations.idiomatic: " Shao said: "A hundred thousand men on a hundred-day round trip will need a hundred days' provisions.

sentences.zh: 頃秋以向末，方欲徵召，兵仗可集，恐糧難至。

translations.literal: Autumn is nearly ended; you are only now about to mobilize. Arms and troops can be gathered, but I fear grain will be hard to deliver.
translations.idiomatic: Autumn is almost over and you are only now mobilizing. Arms and troops can be gathered, but grain may not arrive in time.

sentences.zh: 有兵無糧，何以克敵？

translations.literal: With troops but no grain, how can you defeat the enemy?
translations.idiomatic: With soldiers but no grain, how can you defeat the enemy?

sentences.zh: 願王善思，為社稷深慮。

translations.literal: I hope Your Highness will think carefully and give deep consideration to the altars of state.
translations.idiomatic: I urge Your Highness to think this through carefully for the sake of the realm.

sentences.zh: 」澄沉思良久曰：「實如卿言。

translations.literal: " Cheng pondered long and said: "It is indeed as you say.
translations.idiomatic: " Cheng thought for a long while and said: "You are right.

sentences.zh: 」使還，具以狀聞。

translations.literal: " He sent him back, and Shao reported the full situation.
translations.idiomatic: " Cheng sent him back, and Shao reported everything to the throne.

sentences.zh: 後澄遂征鍾離，無功而返。

translations.literal: Later Cheng did attack Zhongli and returned without success.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng later attacked Zhongli anyway and returned without success.

sentences.zh: 尋除長兼奉車都尉，轉右都水使者，錄事如故。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed acting Chief Commandant of the Imperial Carriages, transferred to Right Envoy of the Directorate of Waterways, and continued as recorder as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made acting Chief Commandant of the Imperial Carriages, then Right Envoy of the Directorate of Waterways, while retaining his post as recorder.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂去職。

translations.literal: Upon his mother's death he left office for mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to mourn his mother.

sentences.zh: 值義陽初復，起紹除寧遠將軍、郢州龍驤府長史，帶義陽太守。

translations.literal: When Yiyang was newly recovered, Shao was recalled and appointed General Who Establishes Peace from Afar, chief clerk of the Dragon-Prancing headquarters in Ying Province, concurrently Administrator of Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Yiyang was newly recovered, Shao was recalled as General Who Establishes Peace from Afar, chief clerk of the Dragon-Prancing headquarters in Ying Province, and concurrent Administrator of Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 其年冬，使還都，值朝廷有南討之計，發河北數州田兵二萬五千人，通緣淮戍兵合五萬餘人，廣開屯田。

translations.literal: That winter, on returning from his mission to the capital, the court was planning a southern campaign; it mobilized twenty-five thousand agricultural soldiers from several northern provinces, and together with garrison troops along the Huai the total exceeded fifty thousand, with garrison farming greatly expanded.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, returning to the capital on mission, he found the court planning a southern campaign: twenty-five thousand farmer-soldiers from the northern provinces were mobilized, and with Huai garrison troops the force exceeded fifty thousand, with garrison farming greatly expanded.

sentences.zh: 八座奏紹為西道六州營田大使，加步兵校尉。

translations.literal: The Eight Ministers memorialized that Shao be made Commissioner for Garrison Farming in the six western provinces, with the additional rank of Colonel of Footsoldiers.
translations.idiomatic: The Eight Ministers recommended Shao as Commissioner for Garrison Farming in the six western provinces, with the additional rank of Colonel of Footsoldiers.

sentences.zh: 紹勤於勸課，頻歲大獲。

translations.literal: Shao was diligent in encouraging farming and for successive years reaped great harvests.
translations.idiomatic: Shao worked diligently to promote farming and reaped abundant harvests year after year.

sentences.zh: 又詔紹詣鍾離，與都督、中山王英論攻鍾離形勢，英固言必克。

translations.literal: An edict also ordered Shao to go to Zhongli and discuss with the commander, Prince of Zhongshan Yuan Ying, the situation for attacking Zhongli; Ying firmly declared it could be taken.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also sent Shao to Zhongli to discuss the attack with Commander Prince of Zhongshan Yuan Ying, who insisted the city would fall.

sentences.zh: 紹觀其城隍防守，恐不可陷，勸令班師，英不從。

translations.literal: Shao observed its walls and defenses and feared it could not be taken; he urged withdrawal, but Ying would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Shao inspected the walls and defenses and judged the city could not be taken; he urged withdrawal, but Ying refused.

sentences.zh: 紹還，具以狀聞。

translations.literal: Shao returned and reported the full situation.
translations.idiomatic: Shao returned and reported everything to the throne.

sentences.zh: 俄而英敗。

translations.literal: Before long Ying was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Ying was defeated.

sentences.zh: 詔以徐豫二境，民稀土曠，令紹量度處所，更立一州。

translations.literal: An edict noted that in the Xu and Yu regions the people were few and the land sparse, and ordered Shao to survey suitable sites and establish a new province.
translations.idiomatic: Because the Xu and Yu regions were sparsely populated, the emperor ordered Shao to survey the territory and establish a new province.

sentences.zh: 紹以譙城形要之所，置州為便，遂立南兗。

translations.literal: Shao held that Qiao city was a strategic place and that establishing the province there would be convenient; Southern Yan Province was therefore created.
translations.idiomatic: Shao judged Qiao city a strategic site and convenient for a provincial seat; Southern Yan Province was therefore established.

sentences.zh: 入為主衣都統，加中堅將軍，轉前軍將軍。

translations.literal: He entered court as Director-in-Chief of the Imperial Wardrobe, was given the additional rank of General of the Central Garrison, and transferred to General of the Forward Army.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court as Director-in-Chief of the Imperial Wardrobe, was made General of the Central Garrison, and then General of the Forward Army.

sentences.zh: 追賞營田之勤，拜游擊將軍。

translations.literal: In recognition of his diligence in garrison farming he was appointed General Who Punishes Bandits.
translations.idiomatic: His diligence in garrison farming was rewarded with appointment as General Who Punishes Bandits.

sentences.zh: 遷龍驤將軍、太府少卿，都統如故。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Dragon-Prancing General and Vice Director of the Imperial Treasury, his directorship remaining as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Dragon-Prancing General and Vice Director of the Imperial Treasury, retaining his directorship.

sentences.zh: 轉長兼太府卿。

translations.literal: He was transferred to acting Director of the Imperial Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: He was made acting Director of the Imperial Treasury.

sentences.zh: 紹量功節用，甄煩就簡，凡有賜給，千匹以上，皆別覆奏，然後出之。

translations.literal: Shao measured merit and economized expenditure, sorting out complexities and reducing them to simplicity; for any grant of a thousand bolts or more, he submitted a separate memorial for approval before releasing it.
translations.idiomatic: Shao measured costs carefully and simplified procedures; any grant of a thousand bolts of silk or more required a separate memorial for approval before disbursement.

sentences.zh: 靈太后嘉其用心，敕紹每月入見，諸有益國利民之事，皆令面陳。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Ling admired his conscientiousness and ordered Shao to enter audience monthly; on all matters benefiting the state and the people, he was to present them in person.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Ling admired his diligence and ordered him to attend audience monthly and present in person anything that would benefit the state and the people.

sentences.zh: 出除安北將軍、并州刺史。

translations.literal: He was sent out and appointed General Who Pacifies the North and Governor of Bing Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed General Who Pacifies the North and Governor of Bing Province.

sentences.zh: 清慎守法，頗得民和。

translations.literal: Upright, cautious, and law-abiding, he won considerable harmony among the people.
translations.idiomatic: Upright, cautious, and law-abiding, he won the people's goodwill.

sentences.zh: 值山胡來寇，不能擊，以此損其聲望。

translations.literal: When the Mountain Hu raided, he could not repel them, and for this his reputation suffered.
translations.idiomatic: When the Mountain Hu raided, he failed to repel them, and his reputation suffered.

sentences.zh: 復入為太府卿。

translations.literal: He again entered court as Director of the Imperial Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to court as Director of the Imperial Treasury.

sentences.zh: 莊帝初，遇害河陰。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Zhuang's reign he was killed at Heyin.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Zhuang's reign he was killed at Heyin.

sentences.zh: 劉桃符，中山盧奴人。

translations.literal: Liu Taofu was a native of Lunu in Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Taofu came from Lunu in Zhongshan commandery.

sentences.zh: 生不識父，九歲喪母。

translations.literal: From birth he never knew his father; at nine he lost his mother.
translations.idiomatic: He never knew his father; his mother died when he was nine.

sentences.zh: 性恭謹，好學。

translations.literal: By nature he was respectful and cautious, and fond of learning.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was respectful, cautious, and devoted to learning.

sentences.zh: 舉孝廉，射策甲科，歷碎職。

translations.literal: Recommended as Filial and Incorrupt, he ranked in the top class in the archery-and-essay examination and passed through minor posts.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended as Filial and Incorrupt, he ranked first in the palace examination and served through a series of minor posts.

sentences.zh: 景明中，羽林監，領主書。

translations.literal: In the Jingming era he was Supervisor of the Feathered Forest and concurrently head clerk.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jingming era he was Supervisor of the Feathered Forest and head clerk.

sentences.zh: 蕭寶夤之降也，桃符受詔迎接。

translations.literal: When Xiao Baoyin surrendered, Taofu received an edict to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Baoyin defected, Taofu was ordered to receive him.

sentences.zh: 歷奉車都尉、長水校尉、游擊將軍。

translations.literal: He served successively as Commandant of the Imperial Carriages, Colonel of the Long River, and General Who Punishes Bandits.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Commandant of the Imperial Carriages, Colonel of the Long River, and General Who Punishes Bandits.

sentences.zh: 正始中，除征虜將軍、中書舍人，以勤明見知。

translations.literal: In the Zhengshi era he was appointed General Who Punishes the Barbarians and Palace Secretariat Attendant, and was recognized for diligence and clarity.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhengshi era he was made General Who Punishes the Barbarians and Palace Secretariat Attendant, and was valued for his diligence and sound judgment.

sentences.zh: 久不遷職，世宗謂之曰：「揚子雲為黃門，頓歷三世。

translations.literal: Long without promotion, Emperor Shizong said to him: "Yang Ziyun served in the Yellow Gate and passed through three reigns in succession.
translations.idiomatic: After long service without promotion, Emperor Xuanwu told him: "Yang Ziyun held the Yellow Gate post through three reigns.

sentences.zh: 卿居此任始十年，不足辭也。

translations.literal: You have held this post for only ten years—hardly grounds for complaint.
translations.idiomatic: You have held this post for only ten years—that is hardly cause for complaint.

sentences.zh: 」東豫州刺史田益宗居邊貪穢，世宗頻詔桃符為使慰喻之。

translations.literal: " Tian Yizong, Governor of Eastern Yu Province, was greedy and corrupt on the frontier; Emperor Shizong repeatedly ordered Taofu as envoy to console and instruct him.
translations.idiomatic: " Tian Yizong, governor of Eastern Yu Province, was corrupt on the frontier; the emperor repeatedly sent Taofu as envoy to admonish him.

sentences.zh: 桃符還，具稱益宗既老耄，而諸子非理處物。

translations.literal: On returning, Taofu reported fully that Yizong was already senile and that his sons handled affairs unreasonably.
translations.idiomatic: On returning, Taofu reported that Yizong was senile and his sons governed unjustly.

sentences.zh: 世宗後欲代之，恐其背叛，拜桃符征虜將軍、豫州刺史，[2]與後軍將軍李世哲領眾襲益宗。

translations.literal: Later the emperor wished to replace him but feared rebellion; he appointed Taofu General Who Punishes the Barbarians and Governor of Yu Province, and together with Rear Army General Li Shizhe led troops in a surprise attack on Yizong.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor later wished to replace him but feared rebellion; he made Taofu General Who Punishes the Barbarians and Governor of Yu Province, and with Rear Army General Li Shizhe led troops against Yizong.

sentences.zh: 語在益宗傳。

translations.literal: The account is given in Yizong's biography.
translations.idiomatic: The full account appears in Yizong's biography.

sentences.zh: 桃符善恤蠻左，為民吏所懷。

translations.literal: Taofu was skilled in caring for the tribal peoples on the left, and was cherished by officials and commoners alike.
translations.idiomatic: Taofu treated the tribal peoples well and was beloved by officials and commoners alike.

sentences.zh: 久之，徵還。

translations.literal: After a long time he was recalled.
translations.idiomatic: After some years he was recalled to court.

sentences.zh: 病卒，年五十一。

translations.literal: He died of illness at the age of fifty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He died of illness at fifty-one.

sentences.zh: 贈後將軍、洛州刺史。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given the rank of Rear General and made Governor of Luo Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Rear General and Governor of Luo Province.

sentences.zh: 子景均，殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: His son Jingjun was an Attending Censor in the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jingjun served as Attending Censor in the Palace.

sentences.zh: 劉道斌，武邑灌津人，自云中山靖王勝之後也。

translations.literal: Liu Daobin was a native of Guanjin in Wuyi and claimed to be a descendant of Prince Jing of Zhongshan, Liu Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Daobin came from Guanjin in Wuyi and claimed descent from Prince Jing of Zhongshan, Liu Sheng.

sentences.zh: 幼而好學，有器幹。

translations.literal: From childhood he loved learning and possessed capacity and resolve.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood he loved learning and showed ability and force of character.

sentences.zh: 及長，腰帶十圍，鬚髯甚美。

translations.literal: When grown, his waist measured ten spans around and his beard and whiskers were very fine.
translations.idiomatic: When grown, his waist measured ten spans around and he wore a magnificent beard.

sentences.zh: 舉孝廉入京，拜校書郎，轉主書，頗為高祖所知。

translations.literal: Recommended as Filial and Incorrupt, he entered the capital and was appointed Proofreader, then head clerk, and came to be well known to Emperor Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended as Filial and Incorrupt, he entered the capital as Proofreader, then head clerk, and came to Emperor Gaozu's notice.

sentences.zh: 從征南陽，還，加積射將軍，給事中。

translations.literal: He followed the campaign against Nanyang; on returning he was given the additional rank of General of Accumulated Arrows and made a Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in the campaign against Nanyang; on returning he was made General of Accumulated Arrows and Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 高祖謂黃門侍郎邢巒曰：「道斌是段之舉，便異儕流矣。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu said to Gentleman of the Yellow Gate Xing Luan: "Daobin is a man of the first rank; he already stands apart from his peers.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu told Gentleman of the Yellow Gate Xing Luan: "Daobin is a man of the first rank—already he stands apart from his peers.

sentences.zh: 」世宗即位，遷謁者僕射。

translations.literal: " When Emperor Shizong took the throne, Daobin was transferred to Supervisor of the Imperial Gate.
translations.idiomatic: " When Emperor Xuanwu succeeded, Daobin was promoted to Supervisor of the Imperial Gate.

sentences.zh: 轉步兵校尉、廣武將軍，領中書舍人。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Colonel of Footsoldiers and General of Broad Might, concurrently Palace Secretariat Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Colonel of Footsoldiers and General of Broad Might, and retained his post as Palace Secretariat Attendant.

sentences.zh: 出為武邑太守。

translations.literal: He was sent out as Administrator of Wuyi.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Administrator of Wuyi.

sentences.zh: 時冀州新經元愉逆亂之後，加以連年災儉，道斌頻為表請，蠲其租賦，百姓賴之。

translations.literal: At that time Ji Province had newly suffered the rebellion of Yuan Yu, and in addition there had been famine year after year; Daobin repeatedly submitted memorials requesting remission of taxes and levies, and the people relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Province had just endured Yuan Yu's rebellion and years of famine; Daobin repeatedly memorialized for tax relief, and the people depended on him.

sentences.zh: 罷郡還，除右將軍、太中大夫。

translations.literal: When he left his commandery and returned, he was appointed General of the Right and Grand Master of Palace Counsel.
translations.idiomatic: On leaving his post he was made General of the Right and Grand Master of Palace Counsel.

sentences.zh: 又以本將軍出為恒農太守，遷岐州刺史，所在有清治之稱。

translations.literal: Again with his former general's rank he was sent out as Administrator of Hengnong, then transferred to Governor of Qi Province; wherever he served he won repute for upright governance.
translations.idiomatic: He was again sent out as Administrator of Hengnong with his former general's rank, then made Governor of Qi Province; everywhere he served he was praised for clean administration.

sentences.zh: 正光四年，卒於州。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhengguang he died in his province.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Zhengguang he died in office.

sentences.zh: 贈平東將軍、滄州刺史，改贈濟州，諡曰康。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given the rank of General Who Pacifies the East and made Governor of Cang Province; this was later changed to Ji Province, with the posthumous title Kang.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as General Who Pacifies the East and Governor of Cang Province, later changed to Ji Province, with the posthumous name Kang.

sentences.zh: 道斌在恒農，修立學館，建孔子廟堂，圖畫形像。

translations.literal: While in Hengnong, Daobin built a school hall, erected a temple to Confucius, and painted his image.
translations.idiomatic: At Hengnong, Daobin founded a school, built a temple to Confucius, and painted his image.

sentences.zh: 去郡之後，民故追思之，乃復畫道斌形於孔子像之西而拜謁焉。

translations.literal: After he left the commandery, the people still remembered him fondly and again painted Daobin's likeness to the west of Confucius's image and made obeisance there.
translations.idiomatic: After he left office, the people still cherished his memory and painted his portrait west of Confucius's image, where they came to pay homage.

sentences.zh: 子士長，武定中，碭郡太守。

translations.literal: His son Shichang, in the Wuding era, was Administrator of Dang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shichang served as Administrator of Dang commandery during the Wuding era.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 董紹，字興遠，新蔡鮦陽人也。

translations.literal: Dong Shao, courtesy name Xingyuan, was a native of Fuyang in Xincai.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Shao, courtesy name Xingyuan, came from Fuyang in Xincai commandery.

sentences.zh: 少好學，頗有文義。

translations.literal: From youth he loved learning and possessed considerable literary understanding.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he loved learning and showed real literary talent.

sentences.zh: 起家四門博士，歷殿中侍御史、國子助教、積射將軍、兼中書舍人。

translations.literal: He began his career as a Erudite of the Four Gates, then served as Attending Censor in the Palace, Assistant Instructor of the Imperial University, General of Accumulated Arrows, and acting Palace Secretariat Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He began as Erudite of the Four Gates, then served as Attending Censor in the Palace, Assistant Instructor of the Imperial University, General of Accumulated Arrows, and acting Palace Secretariat Attendant.

sentences.zh: 辯於對問，為世宗所賞。

translations.literal: Skilled in debate and repartee, he was admired by Emperor Shizong.
translations.idiomatic: Quick in debate, he won Emperor Xuanwu's favor.

sentences.zh: 豫州城人白早生以城南叛，詔紹慰勞。

translations.literal: Bai Zaosheng of Yuzhou city rebelled with the southern part of the city; an edict ordered Shao to console and reassure the region.
translations.idiomatic: When Bai Zaosheng of Yuzhou rebelled with the southern quarter of the city, the emperor sent Shao to console the region.

sentences.zh: 至上蔡，為賊所襲，囚送江東，仍被鎖禁。

translations.literal: When he reached Shangcai he was attacked by rebels, imprisoned, and sent to the lands east of the Yangzi, where he remained in chains.
translations.idiomatic: At Shangcai he was ambushed by rebels, taken prisoner, and sent east of the Yangzi, where he was kept in chains.

sentences.zh: 蕭衍領軍將軍呂僧珍暫與紹言，便相器重。

translations.literal: Xiao Yan's commander-in-chief Lü Sengzhen spoke briefly with Shao and at once held him in esteem.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yan's commander-in-chief Lü Sengzhen spoke with Shao briefly and immediately took a liking to him.

sentences.zh: 衍聞之，遣使勞紹云：「忠臣孝子，不可無人。

translations.literal: When Yan heard of this, he sent an envoy to comfort Shao, saying: "Loyal ministers and filial sons must not be left without recognition.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Yan heard of this, he sent an envoy to comfort Shao, saying: "The realm cannot be without loyal ministers and filial sons.

sentences.zh: 今當聽卿還國。

translations.literal: Now I shall allow you to return to your state.
translations.idiomatic: I shall now allow you to return home.

sentences.zh: 」紹對曰：「老母在洛，無復方寸，既奉恩貸，實若更生。

translations.literal: " Shao replied: "My old mother is in Luoyang; I have no peace of mind. Now that I have received your gracious pardon, it is truly like being born again.
translations.idiomatic: " Shao replied: "My mother is in Luoyang and my mind is in turmoil. Your gracious pardon is like being given life anew.

sentences.zh: 」衍又遣主書霍靈超謂紹曰：「今放卿還，令卿通兩家之好，彼此息民，豈不善也。

translations.literal: " Yan also sent Chief Clerk Huo Lingchao to tell Shao: "Now I release you to return, wishing you to open good relations between our two states so that both sides may give the people rest—is this not excellent?
translations.idiomatic: " Yan also sent Chief Clerk Huo Lingchao to tell Shao: "I release you now so you may restore goodwill between our realms and give both peoples peace—is that not best?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「通好息民，乃兩國之事，既蒙命及，輒當聞奏本朝。

translations.literal: " He replied: "Opening relations and giving the people rest are matters for both states. Having received your command, I shall at once report it to my court.
translations.idiomatic: " He replied: "Peace and goodwill concern both states alike. I have received your charge and shall report it to my court at once.

sentences.zh: 」衍賜紹衣物，引入見之，令其舍人周捨慰勞，并稱：「戰爭多年，民物塗炭，是以不耻先言，與魏朝通好。

translations.literal: " Yan bestowed robes on Shao, led him in for an audience, and had his Attendant Zhou She console him, also saying: "War has lasted for many years and the people lie in ashes; therefore I am not ashamed to speak first of opening relations with the Wei court.
translations.idiomatic: " Yan gave Shao clothing, received him in audience, and had his Attendant Zhou She comfort him, saying: "Years of war have left the people in ruin; that is why I am not ashamed to speak first of peace with Wei.

sentences.zh: 比亦有書，都無報旨。

translations.literal: Recently I also sent a letter, yet received no reply at all.
translations.idiomatic: I sent a letter recently as well, but received no answer.

sentences.zh: 卿宜備申此意，故遣傳詔周靈秀送卿至國，遲有嘉問。

translations.literal: You should fully convey this intent; therefore I send Edict-Bearer Zhou Lingxiu to escort you home, and I await a favorable response.
translations.idiomatic: Convey this fully to your court; I am sending Edict-Bearer Zhou Lingxiu to escort you home and await a favorable reply.

sentences.zh: 」又令謂紹曰：「卿知所以得不死不？

translations.literal: " He also had Shao told: "Do you know why you were not put to death?
translations.idiomatic: " He also asked Shao: "Do you know why you were spared?

sentences.zh: 今者獲卿，乃天意也。

translations.literal: To have captured you now is Heaven's will.
translations.idiomatic: Capturing you now was Heaven's will.

sentences.zh: 夫千人之聚，不散則亂，故須立君以治天下，不以天下養一人。

translations.literal: When a thousand men gather, if they are not dispersed there is disorder; therefore a ruler must be established to govern all under Heaven, and one must not use all under Heaven to sustain a single man.
translations.idiomatic: When a thousand men gather without dispersing, chaos follows; a ruler must govern the realm—the realm exists not to sustain one man alone.

sentences.zh: 凡在民上，胡不思此？

translations.literal: All who stand above the people—why do they not reflect on this?
translations.idiomatic: Why do those who rule the people never reflect on this?

sentences.zh: 若欲通好，今以宿豫還彼，彼當以漢中見歸。

translations.literal: If you wish for good relations, I now return Suyu to you; you in turn should return Hanzhong to me.
translations.idiomatic: If you seek peace, I will return Suyu to you; you must return Hanzhong in exchange.

sentences.zh: 」先是，詔有司以所獲衍將齊苟兒等十人欲以換紹，事在司馬悅傳。

translations.literal: " Earlier, an edict had ordered the relevant offices to exchange the ten captured Liang generals including Qi Gou'er for Shao; the account is given in Sima Yue's biography.
translations.idiomatic: " Earlier the court had ordered an exchange of ten captured Liang generals including Qi Gou'er for Shao; the account appears in Sima Yue's biography.

sentences.zh: 及紹還，世宗愍之，永平中，除給事中，仍兼舍人。

translations.literal: When Shao returned, Emperor Shizong pitied him; in the Yongping era he was appointed Palace Attendant and continued as Attendant concurrently.
translations.idiomatic: When Shao returned, Emperor Xuanwu showed him compassion; during Yongping he was made Palace Attendant and retained his post as Attendant.

sentences.zh: 紹雖陳說和計，朝廷不許。

translations.literal: Although Shao presented plans for peace, the court did not approve.
translations.idiomatic: Though Shao urged a peace settlement, the court refused.

sentences.zh: 久之，加輕車將軍，正舍人，又除步兵校尉。

translations.literal: After a long time he was given the additional rank of General of Light Chariots, made Regular Attendant, and appointed Colonel of Footsoldiers.
translations.idiomatic: After some years he was made General of Light Chariots and Regular Attendant, then Colonel of Footsoldiers.

sentences.zh: 肅宗初，紹上御天馬頌，帝賞其辭，賜帛八十匹。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Suzong's reign, Shao submitted a rhapsody on the Imperial Heavenly Horse; the emperor admired its wording and bestowed eighty bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Xiaoming's reign, Shao submitted a rhapsody on the imperial heavenly horse; the emperor admired it and gave him eighty bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 又除龍驤將軍、中散大夫，舍人如故。

translations.literal: He was again appointed Dragon-Prancing General and Grand Master of Palace Leisure, his post as Attendant remaining as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Dragon-Prancing General and Grand Master of Palace Leisure, retaining his post as Attendant.

sentences.zh: 加冠軍將軍，出除右將軍、洛州刺史。

translations.literal: He was given the additional rank of Champion General and sent out as General of the Right and Governor of Luo Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Champion General and sent out as General of the Right and Governor of Luo Province.

sentences.zh: 紹好行小惠，頗得民情。

translations.literal: Shao liked to dispense small favors and won considerable goodwill among the people.
translations.idiomatic: Shao was fond of small acts of kindness and won the people's goodwill.

sentences.zh: 蕭衍將軍曹義宗、王玄真等寇荊州，據順陽馬圈，裴衍、王羆討之。

translations.literal: Xiao Yan's generals Cao Yizong, Wang Xuanzhen, and others raided Jing Province and seized the horse pastures of Shunyang; Pei Yan and Wang Pi went to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yan's generals Cao Yizong and Wang Xuanzhen raided Jing Province and seized the horse pastures at Shunyang; Pei Yan and Wang Pi marched against them.

sentences.zh: 既復順陽，進圍馬圈。

translations.literal: Having recovered Shunyang, they advanced to besiege the horse pastures.
translations.idiomatic: After recovering Shunyang, they advanced to besiege the horse pastures.

sentences.zh: 城堅，裴王糧少，紹上書言其必敗。

translations.literal: The city was strong, and Pei and Wang had little grain; Shao submitted a memorial saying they were certain to fail.
translations.idiomatic: The fortress was strong and Pei and Wang were short of grain; Shao memorialized that they were bound to fail.

sentences.zh: 未幾，裴衍等果失利，順陽復為義宗所據。

translations.literal: Before long Pei Yan and the others did indeed suffer defeat, and Shunyang was again seized by Yizong.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Pei Yan and his forces were defeated, and Shunyang fell again to Yizong.

sentences.zh: 紹有氣病，啟求解州，詔不許。

translations.literal: Shao suffered from a breathing ailment and petitioned to be relieved of his province; an edict did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Shao suffered from a respiratory ailment and asked to leave his post; the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 蕭寶夤反於長安也，紹上書求擊之，云：「臣當出瞎巴三千，生噉蜀子。

translations.literal: When Xiao Baoyin rebelled at Chang'an, Shao submitted a memorial requesting to attack him, saying: "Your servant will lead out three thousand blind Ba warriors to devour the Shu men alive.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Baoyin rebelled at Chang'an, Shao memorialized asking to attack him, saying: "I will lead three thousand fearless Ba warriors to devour the Shu rebels alive.

sentences.zh: 」肅宗謂黃門徐紇曰：「此巴真瞎也？

translations.literal: " Emperor Suzong said to Gentleman of the Yellow Gate Xu He: "Are these Ba truly blind?
translations.idiomatic: " Emperor Xiaoming asked Gentleman of the Yellow Gate Xu He: "Are these Ba truly blind?

sentences.zh: 」紇曰：「此是紹之壯辭，云巴人勁勇，見敵無所畏懼，非實瞎也。

translations.literal: " Xu He said: "This is Shao's bold rhetoric—he means the Ba are fierce and brave and fear no enemy when they see one; they are not actually blind.
translations.idiomatic: " Xu He said: "That is Shao's bold rhetoric—the Ba are fierce and fearless before the enemy; they are not literally blind.

sentences.zh: 」帝大笑，敕紹速行。

translations.literal: " The emperor laughed loudly and ordered Shao to set out at once.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor laughed and ordered Shao to depart at once.

sentences.zh: 又加平西將軍。

translations.literal: He was also given the additional rank of General Who Pacifies the West.
translations.idiomatic: He was also made General Who Pacifies the West.

sentences.zh: 以拒寶夤之功，賞新蔡縣開國男，食邑二百戶。

translations.literal: For his merit in resisting Baoyin he was enfeoffed as Baron of Xincai county with a fief of two hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: For resisting Baoyin he was enfeoffed as Baron of Xincai with a fief of two hundred households.

translations.literal: Editorial note marker [3] in the received text.
translations.idiomatic: Footnote marker [3] in the received text.

sentences.zh: 永安中，代還。

translations.literal: In the Yongan era he was replaced and recalled.
translations.idiomatic: During Yongan he was replaced and recalled.

sentences.zh: 於是除安西將軍、梁州刺史、假撫軍將軍、兼尚書，為山南行臺，頗有清稱。

translations.literal: He was then appointed General Who Pacifies the West, Governor of Liang Province, acting General Who Pacifies the Army, and concurrent Minister of the Secretariat, serving as Southern Mountains Mobile Headquarters, and won a considerable reputation for upright conduct.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made General Who Pacifies the West, Governor of Liang Province, acting General Who Pacifies the Army, and concurrent Minister of the Secretariat, heading the Southern Mountains Mobile Headquarters, and earned a reputation for clean governance.

sentences.zh: 前廢帝以元孚代之。

translations.literal: The Deposed Former Emperor replaced him with Yuan Fu.
translations.idiomatic: The Deposed Former Emperor replaced him with Yuan Fu.

sentences.zh: 紹至長安，時尒朱天光為關右大行臺，啟紹為大行臺從事、兼吏部尚書，又除征西將軍、金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: When Shao reached Chang'an, Erzhu Tianguang was then Mobile Headquarters commander for the lands west of the Pass; he recommended Shao as staff officer of the Mobile Headquarters and concurrent Minister of Personnel, and Shao was also appointed General Who Punishes the West and Grand Master of the Golden Chariot with Purple Tassel.
translations.idiomatic: When Shao reached Chang'an, Erzhu Tianguang commanded the Mobile Headquarters west of the Pass and appointed Shao as its staff officer and concurrent Minister of Personnel, with the additional ranks of General Who Punishes the West and Grand Master of the Golden Chariot with Purple Tassel.

sentences.zh: 天光赴洛，留紹於後。

translations.literal: Tianguang went to Luoyang and left Shao behind.
translations.idiomatic: Tianguang went to Luoyang and left Shao in the rear.

sentences.zh: 天光敗，賀拔岳復請紹為其開府諮議參軍。

translations.literal: When Tianguang was defeated, Heba Yue again requested Shao as advisory staff officer in his headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: After Tianguang's defeat, Heba Yue again took Shao on as advisory staff officer in his headquarters.

sentences.zh: 永熙中，加車騎將軍。

translations.literal: In the Yongxi era he was given the additional rank of General of Chariots and Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: During Yongxi he was made General of Chariots and Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 岳後攜紹於高平牧馬，紹悲而賦詩曰：「走馬山之阿，馬渴飲黃河，寧謂胡關下，復聞楚客歌。

translations.literal: Later Yue took Shao with him to pasture horses at Gaoping; sorrowfully Shao composed a poem: "Galloping horses on the mountain slope, thirsty horses drink from the Yellow River—who would have thought below the Hu Pass one would again hear a Chu traveler's song?
translations.idiomatic: Later Yue took Shao to pasture horses at Gaoping; in sorrow Shao composed a poem: "Galloping horses on the mountain slope, thirsty horses drink from the Yellow River—who would have thought that below the northern passes one would hear a Chu traveler's song again?

sentences.zh: 」後為宇文黑獺所殺。

translations.literal: " Later he was killed by Yuwen Heita.
translations.idiomatic: " He was later killed by Yuwen Heita.

sentences.zh: 子敏，永安中，為太尉西閤祭酒。

translations.literal: His son Min, in the Yongan era, was Libationer of the Western Pavilion of the Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: His son Min served during Yongan as Libationer of the Western Pavilion of the Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 馮元興，字子盛，東魏郡肥鄉人也。

translations.literal: Feng Yuanxing, courtesy name Zisheng, was a native of Feixiang in Eastern Wei commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Yuanxing, courtesy name Zisheng, came from Feixiang in Eastern Wei commandery.

sentences.zh: 其世父僧集，官至東清河、西平原二郡太守，贈濟州刺史。

translations.literal: His father's elder brother Sengji rose to be Administrator of the two commanderies of Eastern Qinghe and Western Pingyuan and was posthumously made Governor of Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: His father's elder brother Sengji served as Administrator of Eastern Qinghe and Western Pingyuan and was posthumously honored as Governor of Ji Province.

sentences.zh: 元興少有操尚，隨僧集在平原，因就中山張吾貴、常山房虬學，通禮傳，頗有文才。

translations.literal: Yuanxing from youth possessed moral resolve; following Sengji in Pingyuan, he studied under Zhang Wugui of Zhongshan and Fang Qiu of Changshan, mastered the Rites and the Commentary, and possessed considerable literary talent.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Yuanxing showed moral seriousness; while with Sengji in Pingyuan he studied under Zhang Wugui of Zhongshan and Fang Qiu of Changshan, mastered the Rites tradition, and showed real literary talent.

sentences.zh: 年二十三，還鄉教授，常數百人。

translations.literal: At twenty-three he returned home to teach, and his students often numbered in the hundreds.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty-three he returned home to teach, with hundreds of students.

sentences.zh: 領僚孝廉，對策高第，又舉秀才。

translations.literal: He was recommended as Filial and Incorrupt by his district, ranked in the top class in the policy examination, and was also nominated as Outstanding Talent.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended as Filial and Incorrupt by his district, he ranked first in the policy examination and was also nominated as Outstanding Talent.
