sentences.zh: 時御史中尉王顯有權寵，元興奏記於顯，召為檢校御史。

translations.literal: At that time Censor-in-Chief Wang Xian held power and favor; Yuanxing submitted a letter to Xian and was summoned as Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Wang Xian then held power; Yuanxing submitted a letter to him and was summoned as Investigating Censor.

sentences.zh: 尋轉殿中，除奉朝請，三使高麗。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to the Palace Censorate, appointed Court Gentleman for Imperial Audiences, and thrice served as envoy to Goguryeo.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to the Palace Censorate, made Court Gentleman for Imperial Audiences, and served three missions to Goguryeo.

sentences.zh: 江陽王繼為司徒，元興為記室參軍，遂為元叉所知。

translations.literal: When Prince Jiangyang Ji became Minister of Education, Yuanxing was his staff recorder, and thus came to be known to Yuan Cha.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Jiangyang Ji became Minister of Education, Yuanxing served as his staff recorder and came to Yuan Cha's notice.

sentences.zh: 叉秉朝政，引元興為尚書殿中郎，領中書舍人，仍御史。

translations.literal: Cha held the reins of government and brought Yuanxing in as Palace Attendant of the Secretariat, concurrently Palace Secretariat Attendant, while retaining his censor's post.
translations.idiomatic: Cha dominated the government and made Yuanxing Palace Attendant of the Secretariat and Palace Secretariat Attendant while keeping him as censor.

sentences.zh: 元興居其腹心，預聞時事，卑身克己，人無恨焉。

translations.literal: Yuanxing stood at his inner circle, privy to affairs of the day; humble in bearing and self-restrained, he aroused no resentment in others.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanxing stood at Cha's inner circle, privy to state affairs; humble and self-restrained, he aroused no resentment.

sentences.zh: 家素貧約，食客恒數十人，同其飢飽，曾無吝色，時人歎尚之。

translations.literal: His household had always been poor and frugal; he constantly had dozens of guests and shared their hunger and fullness without ever showing stinginess—men of the time admired him for it.
translations.idiomatic: His household was always poor; he kept dozens of guests and shared their fare without stint—men of the time admired him for it.

sentences.zh: 及太保崔光臨薨，薦元興為侍讀。

translations.literal: When Grand Guardian Cui Guang was near death, he recommended Yuanxing as Lecturer-in-Attendance.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand Guardian Cui Guang was dying, he recommended Yuanxing as Lecturer-in-Attendance.

sentences.zh: 尚書賈思伯為侍講，授肅宗杜氏春秋於式乾殿，元興常為摘句，儒者榮之。

translations.literal: Minister Jia Sibo served as Lecturer-in-Explanation and taught Emperor Suzong the Zuo Commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals in the Shiqian Hall; Yuanxing often selected passages, and the Confucian scholars took it as an honor.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Jia Sibo lectured Emperor Xiaoming on the Zuo Commentary in the Shiqian Hall; Yuanxing often selected passages, to the scholars' acclaim.

sentences.zh: 及叉欲解領軍，以訪元興。

translations.literal: When Cha wished to relinquish command of the army, he consulted Yuanxing.
translations.idiomatic: When Cha wished to resign command of the army, he consulted Yuanxing.

sentences.zh: 元興曰：「未知公意如何耳？

translations.literal: Yuanxing said: "I do not yet know what Your Excellency truly intends?
translations.idiomatic: Yuanxing said: "I do not yet know what you truly intend?

sentences.zh: 」叉曰：「卿謂吾欲反也？

translations.literal: " Cha said: "Do you think I mean to rebel?
translations.idiomatic: " Cha said: "Do you think I plan to rebel?

sentences.zh: 」元興不敢言，因勸之。

translations.literal: " Yuanxing dared not speak further and thereupon urged him on.
translations.idiomatic: " Yuanxing said no more and urged him to proceed.

sentences.zh: 叉既賜死，元興亦被廢。

translations.literal: After Cha was ordered to take his own life, Yuanxing was also dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: After Cha was ordered to commit suicide, Yuanxing was dismissed as well.

sentences.zh: 乃為浮萍詩以自喻曰：「有草生碧池，無根綠水上。

translations.literal: He then composed a poem on duckweed to describe himself: "A plant grows in the jade-green pool, rootless on the green water.
translations.idiomatic: He then wrote a poem on duckweed as self-description: "A plant grows in the jade pool, rootless on the green water.

sentences.zh: 脆弱惡風波，危微苦驚浪。」

translations.literal: Frail, it hates wind and waves; in peril and weakness it suffers the shock of surging billows."
translations.idiomatic: Frail, it dreads wind and waves; in peril it suffers every surge."

sentences.zh: 丞相、高陽王雍召為兼屬。

translations.literal: The Chancellor, Prince of Gaoyang Yuan Yong, summoned him as an additional staff member.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Prince of Gaoyang Yuan Yong summoned him as an additional staff member.

sentences.zh: 未幾，去任還鄉。

translations.literal: Before long he left his post and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he left his post and returned home.

sentences.zh: 僕射元羅為東道大使，以元興為本郡太守。

translations.literal: Vice Director Yuan Luo served as envoy of the Eastern Route and made Yuanxing Administrator of his native commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director Yuan Luo, envoy of the Eastern Route, made Yuanxing Administrator of his home commandery.

sentences.zh: 尋徵赴闕。

translations.literal: Soon he was summoned to court.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon summoned to court.

sentences.zh: 以母憂還家，頻值鄉亂，數為監軍，元興多所賞罰，鄉黨頗以此憾焉。

translations.literal: He returned home for his mother's mourning; disturbances in the countryside recurred frequently, and he was several times made army supervisor; Yuanxing dispensed many rewards and punishments, and his neighbors were rather resentful of this.
translations.idiomatic: He returned home to mourn his mother; with repeated local unrest he served several times as army supervisor, meting out many rewards and punishments, to his neighbors' resentment.

sentences.zh: 上黨王天穆之討邢杲，引為大將軍從事中郎。

translations.literal: When Prince of Shangdang Tianmu campaigned against Xing Guo, he took Yuanxing as staff officer of the great general.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Shangdang Tianmu campaigned against Xing Guo, he took Yuanxing on as staff officer of the great general.

sentences.zh: 元顥入洛，復為平北將軍、光祿大夫，領中書舍人。

translations.literal: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, Yuanxing again became General Who Pacifies the North and Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, concurrently Palace Secretariat Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, Yuanxing again became General Who Pacifies the North and Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, and Palace Secretariat Attendant.

sentences.zh: 莊帝還宮，天穆以為太宰諮議參軍，加征虜將軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuang returned to the palace, Tianmu made him advisory staff officer of the Grand Minister of War and gave him the additional rank of General Who Punishes the Barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhuang returned to the palace, Tianmu made him advisory staff officer of the Grand Minister of War with the additional rank of General Who Punishes the Barbarians.

sentences.zh: 普泰初，安東將軍、光祿大夫，領中書舍人。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Putai he was General Who Pacifies the East and Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, concurrently Palace Secretariat Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Putai he was General Who Pacifies the East and Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, and Palace Secretariat Attendant.

sentences.zh: 太昌初，卒於家，贈征東將軍、齊州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taichang he died at home and was posthumously given the rank of General Who Punishes the East and made Governor of Qi Province.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Taichang he died at home and was posthumously honored as General Who Punishes the East and Governor of Qi Province.

sentences.zh: 文集百餘篇。

translations.literal: His collected writings numbered more than a hundred pieces.
translations.idiomatic: He left a collected corpus of more than a hundred pieces.

sentences.zh: 元興世寒，因元叉之勢，託其交道，相用為州主簿，[4]論者以為非倫。

translations.literal: Yuanxing's family had long been poor; relying on Yuan Cha's power, he used their connection to have Xiang Yong appointed chief clerk of the province; critics held this improper.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanxing's family was poor; through Yuan Cha's influence he had Xiang Yong appointed provincial chief clerk—critics judged this improper.

sentences.zh: 高祖時，有譙郡曹道，頗涉經史，有幹用。

translations.literal: In Emperor Gaozu's time there was Cao Dao of Qiao commandery, well versed in the classics and histories and capable in practical affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In Emperor Gaozu's time there was Cao Dao of Qiao commandery, well read in the classics and histories and capable in practical affairs.

sentences.zh: 舉孝廉。

translations.literal: He was recommended as Filial and Incorrupt.
translations.idiomatic: He was recommended as Filial and Incorrupt.

sentences.zh: 太和中，東宮主書、門下錄事。

translations.literal: In the Taihe era he was head clerk of the Eastern Palace and recorder under the Gate.
translations.idiomatic: During Taihe he was head clerk of the Eastern Palace and recorder under the Gate.

sentences.zh: 景明中，尚書都令史，領主書。

translations.literal: In the Jingming era he was chief clerk of the Secretariat and concurrently head clerk.
translations.idiomatic: During Jingming he was chief clerk of the Secretariat and head clerk.

sentences.zh: 後轉中書舍人。

translations.literal: Later he was transferred to Palace Secretariat Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made Palace Secretariat Attendant.

sentences.zh: 行使，每稱旨。

translations.literal: On missions he always met with the emperor's approval.
translations.idiomatic: On missions he always pleased the emperor.

sentences.zh: 出除東郡太守。

translations.literal: He was sent out and appointed Administrator of Dong commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Administrator of Dong commandery.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈儀同三司。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously given the rank of equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously honored with rank equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 又有北海曹昇，亦以學識清立見知。

translations.literal: There was also Cao Sheng of Beihai, likewise known for his learning and upright bearing.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Cao Sheng of Beihai, likewise known for learning and upright character.

sentences.zh: 歷治書侍御史。

translations.literal: He served as Attending Censor for Legal Documents.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Attending Censor for Legal Documents.

sentences.zh: 永安中，黃門郎、散騎常侍。

translations.literal: In the Yongan era he was Gentleman of the Yellow Gate and Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: During Yongan he was Gentleman of the Yellow Gate and Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 出帝世，國子祭酒。

translations.literal: In the reign of the Departure Emperor he was Libationer of the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Departure Emperor he was Libationer of the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 不營家產，至以餒卒於鄴，時人傷歎之。

translations.literal: He did not build up family property and in the end died of hunger at Ye; men of the time mourned him.
translations.idiomatic: He built no family fortune and died of hunger at Ye; contemporaries mourned him.

sentences.zh: 又齊郡曹昂，有學識，舉秀才。

translations.literal: There was also Cao Ang of Qi commandery, learned and nominated as Outstanding Talent.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Cao Ang of Qi commandery, a learned man nominated as Outstanding Talent.

sentences.zh: 永安中，太學博士、兼尚書郎。

translations.literal: In the Yongan era he was Erudite of the Imperial University and acting Gentleman of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: During Yongan he was Erudite of the Imperial University and acting Gentleman of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 而常徒步上省，以示清貧。

translations.literal: Yet he often went on foot to the provincial offices to display his poverty and integrity.
translations.idiomatic: He often walked to the offices on foot to display his poverty and integrity.

sentences.zh: 忽遇盜，大失綾縑，時人鄙其矯詐。

translations.literal: Suddenly he met with robbers and lost a great quantity of silk; men of the time despised his pretense and deceit.
translations.idiomatic: Robbers struck and he lost a great quantity of silk; contemporaries despised his affectation.

sentences.zh: 鹿悆，字永吉，濟陰人。

translations.literal: Lu Yu, courtesy name Yongji, was a native of Jiyin.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yu, courtesy name Yongji, came from Jiyin.

sentences.zh: 父生，在良吏傳。

translations.literal: His father Sheng is recorded in the biography of worthy officials.
translations.idiomatic: His father Sheng has a biography among the worthy officials.

sentences.zh: 悆好兵書、陰陽、釋氏之學。

translations.literal: Yu loved books on warfare, yin-yang studies, and Buddhist learning.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was devoted to military texts, yin-yang lore, and Buddhist learning.

sentences.zh: 太師、彭城王勰召為館客。

translations.literal: Grand Tutor, Prince of Pengcheng Xie, summoned him as a lodge guest.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Tutor Prince of Pengcheng Xie took him on as a lodge guest.

sentences.zh: 嘗詣徐州，馬疫，附船而至大梁。

translations.literal: Once when he went to Xuzhou his horse fell ill, and he took a boat to reach Daliang.
translations.idiomatic: Once on a journey to Xuzhou his horse fell ill, and he took a boat to Daliang.

sentences.zh: 夜睡，從者上岸竊禾四束以飼其馬。

translations.literal: He slept at night while his attendants went ashore and stole four sheaves of grain to feed his horse.
translations.idiomatic: He slept while his attendants went ashore and stole four sheaves of grain to feed his horse.

sentences.zh: 船行數里，悆覺，問得禾之處，從者以告。

translations.literal: After the boat had gone several li, Yu awoke, asked where the grain had been taken, and his attendants told him.
translations.idiomatic: After the boat had gone several li, Yu woke, asked where the grain had been taken, and his attendants told him.

sentences.zh: 悆大忿，即停船上岸，至取禾處，以縑三丈置禾束下而返。

translations.literal: Yu was greatly angered, immediately stopped the boat and went ashore to the place where the grain had been taken, placed three zhang of silk beneath the sheaves, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was furious; he stopped the boat, went ashore to the spot, left three zhang of silk under the sheaves as payment, and returned.

sentences.zh: 初為真定公元子直國中尉，恒勸以忠廉之節。

translations.literal: At first he was commandant of the principality of Prince Zizhi of Zhending, Yuan Yuan, and constantly urged him to observe the principles of loyalty and integrity.
translations.idiomatic: He first served as commandant of the principality of Prince Zizhi of Zhending and constantly urged him to loyalty and integrity.

sentences.zh: 嘗賦五言詩曰：「嶧山萬丈樹，雕鏤作琵琶。

translations.literal: He once composed a five-character poem saying: "A ten-thousand-zhang tree on Mount Yi, carved and inlaid to make a pipa.
translations.idiomatic: He once wrote a five-character poem: "A tree ten thousand zhang tall on Mount Yi, carved and inlaid into a pipa.

sentences.zh: 由此材高遠，弦響藹中華。

translations.literal: From this, talent lofty and far-reaching; the string's sound suffuses the Central Realm.
translations.idiomatic: Thus talent rises high and far, and the music's resonance fills all the land.

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「援琴起何調？

translations.literal: " Again it says: "Taking up the zither, what mode does one begin?
translations.idiomatic: " It continues: "When you draw the qin to play, what tune will you raise?

sentences.zh: 幽蘭與白雪。

translations.literal: Orchid-in-the-Depths and White Snow.
translations.idiomatic: The Hidden Orchid or White Snow?

sentences.zh: 絲管韻未成，莫使弦響絕。

translations.literal: Silk and pipe—the melody is not yet formed; do not let the string's sound cease.
translations.idiomatic: Let the music find its form before the last note dies away.

sentences.zh: 」子直少有令問，悆欲其善終，故以諷焉。

translations.literal: " Yuan Zizhi from youth had a fine reputation; Yu wished him a good end, and therefore admonished him with this.
translations.idiomatic: " Yuan Zizhi had enjoyed an excellent reputation since youth, and Yu offered these lines in the hope that he would finish well.

sentences.zh: 母憂去職。

translations.literal: On his mother's bereavement he left his post.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned when mourning his mother.

sentences.zh: 服闋，仍卒任。

translations.literal: When the mourning period ended, he resumed and completed his appointment.
translations.idiomatic: After the mourning term, he returned and finished out his term of office.

sentences.zh: 子直出鎮梁州，悆隨之州。

translations.literal: When Zizhi went out to govern Liang Province, Yu followed him to that province.
translations.idiomatic: When Zizhi was posted to Liang Province, Yu accompanied him there.

sentences.zh: 州有兵糧和糴，和糴者靡不潤屋，悆獨不取，子直強之，終不從命。

translations.literal: The province had coordinated grain purchases for military provisions; those who engaged in coordinated purchase without exception enriched their households—but Yu alone took nothing. Zizhi pressed him, yet in the end he would not obey the order.
translations.idiomatic: The province ran government grain purchases for the army, and officials who handled them invariably grew rich—yet Yu refused to take a share, and though Zizhi insisted, Lu Yu never yielded.

sentences.zh: 莊帝為御史中尉，悆兼殿中侍御史，監臨淮王彧軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuang was Censor-in-Chief, Yu concurrently served as Palace Attendant Censor, supervising the army of Prince Huaiyang Yuan Ye.
translations.idiomatic: While Emperor Zhuang held the post of Censor-in-Chief, Yu was also appointed Palace Attendant Censor, with oversight of Prince Huaiyang Yuan Ye's forces.

sentences.zh: 時蕭衍遣其豫章王綜據徐州，綜密信通彧，云欲歸款。

translations.literal: At that time Xiao Yan sent his Prince of Yuzhang, Zong, to hold Xuzhou; Zong sent secret letters to Ye, saying he wished to submit in good faith.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Xiao Yan had placed his son, Prince Zong of Yuzhang, in command at Xuzhou, and Zong sent covert messages to Yuan Ye offering to defect.

sentences.zh: 綜時為蕭衍愛子，眾議咸謂不然。

translations.literal: Zong was then Xiao Yan's beloved son, and general opinion unanimously held that this could not be so.
translations.idiomatic: Since Zong was Xiao Yan's favored son, nearly everyone dismissed the report as impossible.

sentences.zh: 彧募人入報，驗其虛實，悆遂請行，曰：「若綜有誠心，與之盟約；

translations.literal: Ye recruited men to enter and report back, to verify whether the claim was true or false; Yu then requested to go, saying: "If Zong has sincere intent, I shall make a pact with him;
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Ye sought volunteers to go in and confirm the truth of the matter, and Yu offered himself, saying, "If Zong is sincere, I will treat with him and bind our agreement;

sentences.zh: 如其詐也，豈惜一人命也。

translations.literal: if it is deception, what is one man's life that it should be spared?
translations.idiomatic: and if this is a trap, what is one life against the chance to learn the truth?

sentences.zh: 」時徐州始陷，邊方騷擾，綜部將成景儁、胡龍牙並總強兵，內外嚴固。

translations.literal: " At that time Xuzhou had just fallen; the border regions were in turmoil; Zong's subordinate generals Cheng Jingjun and Hu Longya both commanded strong troops, and inner and outer defenses were tightly held.
translations.idiomatic: " Xuzhou had only recently been lost and the frontier was unsettled; Zong's generals Cheng Jingjun and Hu Longya commanded sizable forces, and the city's defenses were strong inside and out.

sentences.zh: 悆遂單馬間出，徑趣彭城。

translations.literal: Yu then rode out alone by secret routes, pressing straight for Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yu set out alone on horseback by back roads, heading straight for Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 未至之間，為綜軍主程兵潤所止，問其來狀。

translations.literal: Before he arrived, he was stopped by Zong's army commander Cheng Bingrun, who questioned him as to the purpose of his coming.
translations.idiomatic: Before he reached the city, he was intercepted by Zong's officer Cheng Bingrun, who questioned his purpose.

sentences.zh: 悆答曰：「兵交使在，自昔通言。

translations.literal: Yu replied: "When armies clash, envoys remain—since antiquity messages have passed between them.
translations.idiomatic: Yu answered, "Envoys have always moved between hostile camps—it is an ancient custom.

sentences.zh: 我為臨淮王所使，須有交易。

translations.literal: I am sent by Prince Huaiyang; there is business that must be transacted.
translations.idiomatic: I come on Prince Huaiyang's orders and have urgent business to discuss.

sentences.zh: 」兵潤遂先遣人白龍牙等。

translations.literal: " Bingrun then first sent men ahead to inform Hu Longya and the others.
translations.idiomatic: " Bingrun immediately sent word ahead to Hu Longya and the others.

sentences.zh: 綜既有誠心，聞悆被執，語景儁等曰：「我每疑元略規欲叛城，將驗其虛實，且遣左右為元略使入魏軍中，喚彼一人，其使果至。

translations.literal: Since Zong genuinely intended submission, when he heard Yu had been detained, he told Jingjun and the others: "I have often suspected Yuan Lue of plotting to betray the city; I wished to test whether this was real, and sent attendants disguised as Yuan Lue's envoys into the Wei army to summon one man—and the envoy indeed came.
translations.idiomatic: Zong's intent was genuine; learning that Yu had been seized, he told Jingjun and his colleagues, "I have long suspected Yuan Lue of planning to hand over the city. To test whether the Wei side was serious, I sent men posing as Yuan Lue's envoys to summon a representative—and the envoy actually came.

sentences.zh: 可令人詐作略身，在一深室，詭為患狀，呼使戶外，令人傳語。

translations.literal: One can have a man falsely impersonate Lue's person, in a deep inner chamber, feigning illness, call the envoy outside the door, and have another relay the words.
translations.idiomatic: Have someone impersonate Lue, shut away in an inner room as if ill, and speak to the envoy from beyond the door through an intermediary.

sentences.zh: 」時略始被衍追還。

translations.literal: " At that time Lue had just been recalled by Yan.
translations.idiomatic: " By then Xiao Yan had already recalled Yuan Lue.

sentences.zh: 綜又遣腹心梁話迎悆，密語意狀，令善酬答，引悆入城，詣龍牙所。

translations.literal: Zong again sent his trusted man Liang Hua to welcome Yu, privately conveying the situation and instructing him to reply well; he led Yu into the city to Longya's residence.
translations.idiomatic: Zong then sent his confidant Liang Hua to receive Yu, briefing him privately on how to respond, and escorted him into the city to Hu Longya's quarters.

sentences.zh: 時日已暮，龍牙列仗舉火引悆曰：「元中山甚欲相見，故令喚卿。

translations.literal: The day was already late; Longya arrayed troops, raised torches, and led Yu forward, saying: "Yuan Zhongshan greatly wishes to meet you, and therefore ordered me to summon you.
translations.idiomatic: By then evening had fallen. Hu Longya drew up his guard, lit torches, and led Yu in, saying, "Yuan Zhongshan is eager to see you and has sent for you.

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「安豐、臨淮將少弱卒，規復此城，容可得乎！

translations.literal: " He also said: "The generals of Anfeng and Huaiyang lead few weak troops and plan to recover this city—might that possibly succeed!
translations.idiomatic: " He added, "The Wei forces at Anfeng and Huaiyang are weak in number—do you really think they can retake this city?

sentences.zh: 」悆曰：「彭城魏之東鄙，勢在必爭，得否在天，非人所測。

translations.literal: " Yu said: "Pengcheng is Wei's eastern frontier—contention is inevitable; whether it is taken rests with Heaven, not within human reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: " Yu replied, "Pengcheng is the eastern gateway of Wei and both sides must fight for it. Whether it falls is fate's matter, not ours to foretell.

sentences.zh: 」龍牙曰：「當如卿言。

translations.literal: " Longya said: "It should be as you say.
translations.idiomatic: " Longya said, "No doubt you are right.

sentences.zh: 」復詣景儁住所，停悆在外門，久而未入。

translations.literal: " He again went to Jingjun's lodging; Yu was kept at the outer gate and for a long time was not admitted.
translations.idiomatic: " They then went to Cheng Jingjun's residence, where Yu was held at the outer gate for quite some time before being admitted.

sentences.zh: 時夜已久，星月甚明。

translations.literal: The night was already far advanced; stars and moon were very bright.
translations.idiomatic: It was late at night, under a clear, bright sky.

sentences.zh: 有綜軍主姜桃來與悆語曰：「君年已長宿，又充今使，良有所達。

translations.literal: A Zong army commander, Jiang Tao, came to speak with Yu, saying: "Sir, your years are already advanced and seasoned; moreover you fill the present envoy's role—you surely understand much.
translations.idiomatic: One of Zong's officers, Jiang Tao, came to speak with him and said, "You are a man of age and experience, and you come as an envoy—you must see things clearly.

sentences.zh: 元法僧魏之微子，拔城歸梁，梁主待物有道。

translations.literal: Yuan Faseng was a minor son of Wei; he pulled up the city and returned to Liang, and the Liang lord treats men with principle.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Faseng was a lesser prince of Wei who surrendered his city to Liang, and the Liang emperor knows how to reward such men.

sentences.zh: 」乃舉手上指：「今歲星在斗。

translations.literal: " He then raised his hand and pointed upward: "This year the year-star is in Dipper.
translations.idiomatic: " He lifted a hand toward the sky: "This year the Year Star sits in the Dipper.

sentences.zh: 斗，吳之分野，君何為不歸梁國，我令君富貴。

translations.literal: Dipper is Wu's allotted territory—why do you not return to the Liang state? I will make you rich and honored.
translations.idiomatic: The Dipper is Wu's celestial domain. Why not come over to Liang? I can make you wealthy.

sentences.zh: 」悆答曰：「君徒知其一，未知其二。

translations.literal: " Yu replied: "You know only the one and do not know the second.
translations.idiomatic: " Yu answered, "You see one side of the matter, not the other.

sentences.zh: 法僧者，莒僕之流，而梁納之，無乃有愧於季孫也？

translations.literal: Faseng is of the sort of Ju's servant-boy—yet Liang received him; is there not reason to feel shame before Ji Sun?
translations.idiomatic: Faseng is the sort of renegade Ji Sun would have despised—does Liang feel no shame in sheltering him?

sentences.zh: 今月建鶉首，斗牛受破，歲星木也，逆而克之。

translations.literal: Now the month is established at Quail's Head; Dipper and Ox receive defeat—the year-star is wood, and in opposition it overcomes.
translations.idiomatic: This month falls under the Quail's Head asterism, and the Dipper and Ox are under attack—the Wood star moves contrary to them and will overcome them.

sentences.zh: 君吳國敗喪不久。

translations.literal: Your Wu state's defeat and ruin will come soon.
translations.idiomatic: Defeat for your southern realm is not far off.

sentences.zh: 且衣錦夜遊，有識不許。

translations.literal: Moreover, to wear brocade and roam by night—men of discernment do not approve.
translations.idiomatic: And besides, no wise man praises the vanity of parading in finery by night.

sentences.zh: 」言未及盡，引入見景儁，景儁曰：「元中山雖曰相喚，不懼而來何也？

translations.literal: " Before his words were fully spoken, he was led in to see Jingjun. Jingjun said: "Although Yuan Zhongshan is said to have summoned you, why did you come without fear?
translations.idiomatic: " Before he could finish, he was ushered in to see Cheng Jingjun, who said, "Yuan Zhongshan sent for you—yet you entered his camp without hesitation. Why?

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「昔楚伐吳，吳遣蹷由勞師，今者此行，略同於彼。

translations.literal: " He replied: "Formerly when Chu attacked Wu, Wu sent Jue You to weary the army; the present journey is broadly the same as that.
translations.idiomatic: " He replied, "When Chu once marched against Wu, Wu sent Jue You to wear down the enemy—a mission much like mine today.

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「遊歷多年，與卿先經相識。

translations.literal: " He also said: "For many years I have traveled about—I knew you before.
translations.idiomatic: " He added, "I have traveled widely for years and believe we have met before.

sentences.zh: 」仍敍由緣，景儁便記。

translations.literal: " He then narrated how they had met, and Jingjun took note.
translations.idiomatic: " He recounted their prior acquaintance, and Jingjun wrote it down.

sentences.zh: 引悆同坐，謂悆曰：「卿不為刺客也？

translations.literal: He led Yu to sit together with him and said to Yu: "You are not an assassin, are you?
translations.idiomatic: He invited Yu to sit beside him and asked, "You are not here as an assassin, are you?

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「今者為使，欲返命本朝，相刺之事，更卜後圖。

translations.literal: " He replied: "I am now an envoy and wish to report back to my court; as for stabbing one another, let us choose another time.
translations.idiomatic: " He answered, "I am an envoy on state business and must return with my report. As for killing, that can wait for another day.

sentences.zh: 」為設飯食雜果，悆強飲多食，向敵數人，微自夸矜。

translations.literal: " Food and assorted fruits were set out; Yu drank heartily and ate much, facing several foes, slightly boasting of himself.
translations.idiomatic: " They served a meal with fruit. Yu ate and drank freely, facing down several hostile officers with a touch of swagger.

sentences.zh: 諸人相謂曰：「壯士哉！

translations.literal: The men said to one another: "What a bold warrior!
translations.idiomatic: The others murmured among themselves, "A true bold spirit!

sentences.zh: 」乃引向元略所，一人引入戶內，指床令坐。

translations.literal: " They then led him toward Lue's place; one man brought him inside the door, pointed to a bed, and told him to sit.
translations.idiomatic: " They then took him to Yuan Lue's quarters, where a man ushered him inside and directed him to a seat on the bed.

sentences.zh: 一人別在室中，出謂悆曰：「中山有教，與君相聞。

translations.literal: One man was separately in the chamber; he came out and said to Yu: "Zhongshan has instructions—he wishes to communicate with you.
translations.idiomatic: Another man waited in the adjoining room and came out to say, "Zhongshan sends word and wishes to speak with you.

sentences.zh: 」悆遂起立。

translations.literal: " Yu thereupon rose to his feet.
translations.idiomatic: " Lu Yu immediately stood up.

sentences.zh: 使人謂悆曰：「君但坐。

translations.literal: A messenger told Yu: "Sir, only sit.
translations.idiomatic: The intermediary told him, "Please remain seated.

sentences.zh: 」悆曰：「家國王子，豈有坐聽教命。

translations.literal: " Yu said: "A prince of family and state—how could one sit and listen to instructions?
translations.idiomatic: " Yu said, "He is a prince of our house and realm—how could I sit while he addressed me from afar?

sentences.zh: 」使人曰：「頓首君，我昔有以向南，旦遣相喚，欲聞鄉事。

translations.literal: " The messenger said: "I bow my head to you, sir. Formerly I had reason to turn south; this morning I sent to summon you, wishing to hear news of our homeland.
translations.idiomatic: " The voice from the next room said, "I bow to you, sir. I had matters requiring me to look southward and sent for you this morning to hear news from home.

sentences.zh: 晚來患動，不獲相見。

translations.literal: Tonight my illness flared up, and I could not meet you.
translations.idiomatic: My illness worsened this evening, and I could not receive you in person.

sentences.zh: 」悆曰：「旦奉音旨，冒險祇赴，不得瞻見，內懷反側。

translations.literal: " Yu said: "This morning I received your message and, braving danger, came in respectful attendance; I could not behold you face to face, and within I am unsettled.
translations.idiomatic: " Yu replied, "I obeyed your summons at dawn and came through peril to answer you. Unable to see you, my heart is troubled.

sentences.zh: 」遂辭而退。

translations.literal: " He then took leave and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: " With that he bowed out and left.

sentences.zh: 須臾天曉，綜軍主范勗、景儁、司馬楊㬓等競問北朝士馬多少。

translations.literal: In a little while dawn broke; Zong's army commanders Fan Xu, Jingjun, and Chief Commandant Yang Jun and others competed in asking how many soldiers and horses the Northern Court had.
translations.idiomatic: Before long daylight came, and Zong's officers Fan Xu, Cheng Jingjun, Chief Commandant Yang Jun, and others eagerly asked how large the Northern armies were.

sentences.zh: 悆云：「秦隴既平，三方靜晏，今有高車、白眼、羌、蜀五十萬，齊王、李陳留、[5]崔延伯、李叔仁等分為三道，徑趣江西；

translations.literal: Yu said: "Qin and Long are already pacified; the three regions are calm and settled. Now there are five hundred thousand men of Gaoche, Baiyan, Qiang, and Shu; the Prince of Qi, Li of Chenliu, Editorial note marker [5] in the received text. Cui Yanbo, Li Shuren, and others are divided into three columns, pressing straight toward the lands west of the Yang.
translations.idiomatic: Yu told them, "With Qin and Long secure and the empire quiet, five hundred thousand troops of the Gaoche, Baiyan, Qiang, and Shu peoples are now advancing in three columns led by the Prince of Qi, Li of Chenliu, Footnote marker [5] in the received text. Cui Yanbo, and Li Shuren, marching directly on the territory west of the Yangzi;

sentences.zh: 安樂王鑒、李神領冀、相、齊、濟、青、光羽林十萬，直向琅邪南出。

translations.literal: Prince Anle Jian and Li Shen lead one hundred thousand Feathered Forest troops of Ji, Xiang, Qi, Ji, Qing, and Guang, pressing straight southward out of Langye.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Anle Jian and Li Shen are leading one hundred thousand imperial guards from Ji, Xiang, Qi, Ji, Qing, and Guang provinces in a direct thrust south from Langye.

sentences.zh: 」諸人相謂曰：「詎非華辭也？

translations.literal: " The men said to one another: "Surely these are not flowery words?
translations.idiomatic: " The officers whispered to one another, "Surely this is empty boasting?

sentences.zh: 」悆曰：「可驗崇朝，何華之有！

translations.literal: " Yu said: "They can be verified by morning—what flowery words are there!
translations.idiomatic: " Yu said, "You will see by tomorrow whether I speak truth—there is nothing hollow in it!

sentences.zh: 」日晏令還。

translations.literal: " When the day waned, they ordered him to return.
translations.idiomatic: " At day's end they sent him back.

sentences.zh: 景儁送悆上戲馬臺，北望城壘，曰：「何此城之固，良非彼軍士所能圖擬，卿可語二王，回師改計。

translations.literal: Jingjun escorted Yu up the Play-Horse Terrace, gazed north at the ramparts, and said: "How solid this city is—it is truly not something those enemy soldiers can aspire to match. You may tell the two princes to withdraw their armies and change their plan.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Jingjun walked Lu Yu up to the Play-Horse Terrace and, looking north over the fortifications, said, "See how strong this city is—those Wei troops could never take it. Tell your two princes to abandon the attempt.

sentences.zh: 」悆曰：「金墉湯池，衝甲彌巧，貴守以人，何論險害。

translations.literal: " Yu said: "Gold ramparts and boiling moats—the assault armor grows ever more ingenious; what matters is the men who defend—why speak only of terrain's hazards?
translations.idiomatic: " Yu replied, "Walls and moats mean little—siege craft grows ever cleverer. A city's strength lies in its defenders, not in its terrain.

sentences.zh: 」還軍，於路與梁話誓盟。

translations.literal: " On the return journey he swore an oath and alliance with Liang Hua along the way.
translations.idiomatic: " On the march home he bound himself in covenant with Liang Hua.

sentences.zh: 契約既固，未旬，綜果降。

translations.literal: Once the agreement was firm, within ten days Zong indeed surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: The pact held, and within ten days Zong surrendered as promised.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「日者，法僧父子，頑固自天，長惡不已，竊城外叛，職此亂階，遂使彭宋名藩，翻為賊有。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Lately, Faseng father and son, stubborn by nature, long indulged in evil without cease, stole the city and rebelled outside the walls—through them the ladder of disorder arose—so that Peng and Song, famed frontier commanderies, in turn became the rebels' possession.
translations.idiomatic: An edict read: "Recently Faseng and his son, incorrigible by nature, persisted in wickedness, seized the city, and rebelled—setting chaos in motion and handing the prized fortresses of Peng and Song over to the enemy.

sentences.zh: 雖宗臣名將，揮戈於泗濱；

translations.literal: Although honored ministers and famed generals swung their spears at the Si River's banks;
translations.idiomatic: Though loyal ministers and famed generals fought fiercely along the Si River;

sentences.zh: 虎士雄卒，竦劍於汴渚。

translations.literal: tiger warriors and bold troops stood with swords raised at the Bian River's islets.
translations.idiomatic: and brave soldiers stood ready with swords drawn on the banks of the Bian;

sentences.zh: 然高墉峻堞，非可易登；

translations.literal: yet high walls and lofty battlements are not easily climbed;
translations.idiomatic: still the high walls and steep parapets could not be taken easily;

sentences.zh: 廣涘深隍，實為難踐。

translations.literal: broad moat-shores and deep ditches were truly hard to cross.
translations.idiomatic: and the wide moats and deep trenches proved nearly impassable.

sentences.zh: 是用日昃忘食，中宵憤惋者也。

translations.literal: For this reason the sun slanted and food was forgotten; at midnight there was indignant grief.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor worked past sunset without eating and brooded in anger far into the night.

sentences.zh: 而衍都督、豫章王蕭綜體運知機，欲歸有道，潛遣密信，送款於都督臨淮王。

translations.literal: Yet Yan's Area Commander, Prince of Yuzhang Xiao Zong, by body and fate knew the moment, wished to return to the Way, secretly sent confidential letters, and offered submission to Area Commander Prince Huaiyang.
translations.idiomatic: But Xiao Yan's area commander, Prince Zong of Yuzhang, read the times wisely, wished to submit to legitimate rule, and sent secret letters offering allegiance to Area Commander Prince Huaiyang Yuan Ye.

sentences.zh: 于時事同夜光，能不按劍。

translations.literal: At that time the matter was like a jewel in the night—who could fail to grasp the sword-hilt?
translations.idiomatic: At such a moment, who could sit idle with hand on sword-hilt?

sentences.zh: 殿中侍御史監軍鹿悆，不憚虎口，視險若夷，便能占募，入驗虛實。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Censor supervising the army, Lu Yu, did not fear the tiger's maw, regarded peril as level ground, and at once undertook the mission, entering to verify truth and falsehood.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Censor and army supervisor Lu Yu, undaunted by mortal danger, treated the risk as nothing, volunteered for the mission, and went in to learn the truth.

sentences.zh: 誓盟既固，所圖遂果。

translations.literal: Once the sworn alliance was firm, the design was duly achieved.
translations.idiomatic: The sworn pact held, and the plan succeeded.

sentences.zh: 返地復城，息我兵甲，亦是悆之力焉。

translations.literal: Returning the territory and recovering the city, resting our arms and armor—this too was Yu's power at work.
translations.idiomatic: Recovering the land and city and sparing our armies was also Lu Yu's doing.

sentences.zh: 若不酬以榮祿，何以勸厲將來，可封定陶縣開國子，食邑三百戶。」

translations.literal: If he is not rewarded with honored salary, how can the future be urged and encouraged? He may be enfeoffed as Viscount of Dingtao with a fief of three hundred households."
translations.idiomatic: If such service goes unrewarded, what lesson would future officers draw? Let him be enfeoffed as Viscount of Dingtao with three hundred taxable households."

sentences.zh: 除員外散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He was appointed Outside-section Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Outside-section Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 俄出為青州彭城王劭府長兼司馬。

translations.literal: Soon he went out as Chief of the Pengcheng Prince Shao's Qing Province headquarters, concurrently serving as Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was posted as chief administrator and concurrent commandant in the Qing Province headquarters of Prince Shao of Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 尋解長兼。

translations.literal: Before long he was released from the concurrent chief post.
translations.idiomatic: He soon relinquished the concurrent chief administrator role.

sentences.zh: 廣川人劉鈞、東清河人房須反，[6]劭遣悆監州軍討之，戰於商山，頗有所捷。

translations.literal: Liu Jun of Guangchuan and Fang Xu of East Qinghe rebelled. Editorial note marker [6] in the received text. Shao sent Yu to supervise the provincial army in suppressing them; they fought at Shangshan and achieved considerable success.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jun of Guangchuan and Fang Xu of East Qinghe rose in rebellion. Footnote marker [6] in the received text. Prince Shao dispatched Yu to command the provincial forces against them, and at Shangshan they won notable success.

sentences.zh: 將統皆劭左右，擅增首級，妄請賞帛，悆面執不與，劭弗從。

translations.literal: The generals and commanders were all Shao's close associates; they on their own inflated head counts and recklessly requested reward silks; Yu openly held firm and would not grant them, but Shao did not heed him.
translations.idiomatic: The field commanders were Prince Shao's favorites; they inflated their kill counts and demanded bounty silk, which Yu refused to authorize—yet Shao sided against him.

sentences.zh: 悆勃然作色曰：「竭志立言，為王為國，豈悆家事！

translations.literal: Yu suddenly flushed with anger and said: "I exhaust my will and stand on my words—for the prince, for the state—is this Yu's private household affair!
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yu flushed with anger and said, "I speak my mind and serve the prince and the realm—this is not some private family matter of mine!

sentences.zh: 」不辭而出，劭追而謝焉。

translations.literal: " Without taking leave he went out; Shao pursued him and apologized.
translations.idiomatic: " He stalked out without farewell, and Prince Shao followed to apologize.

sentences.zh: 竊勳者放言噂𠴲，欲加私害，悆聞而笑之，不以介意。

translations.literal: Those who had stolen merit spread slanderous talk, wishing to do him private harm; Yu heard and laughed, not taking it to heart.
translations.idiomatic: Those who had embezzled credit for themselves spread gossip hoping to harm him, but Yu only laughed and paid it no mind.

sentences.zh: 先是，蕭衍遣將彭羣、王辯率眾七萬圍逼琅邪。

translations.literal: Earlier, Xiao Yan sent generals Peng Qun and Wang Bian to lead seventy thousand men in besieging Langye.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Xiao Yan had sent Peng Qun and Wang Bian with seventy thousand men to press Langye.

sentences.zh: 自春及秋，官軍不至，而兩青士馬，裁可萬餘，師次鄖城，[7]久而未進。

translations.literal: From spring to autumn the government army did not arrive; yet in the two Qing provinces soldiers and horses amounted to only somewhat more than ten thousand; the army halted at Yuncheng, Editorial note marker [7] in the received text. and for a long time did not advance.
translations.idiomatic: From spring through autumn no relief force came, while Qing Province could field barely ten thousand troops, camped at Yuncheng. Footnote marker [7] in the received text. For a long time they did not advance.

sentences.zh: 劭乃遣悆，南青州刺史胡平遣長史劉仁之，並監勒諸將，徑赴賊壘，大破之，斬羣首，俘馘二千餘級。

translations.literal: Shao thereupon sent Yu; the Southern Qing Province Governor Hu Ping sent his Chief Clerk Liu Renzhi; together they supervised and drove the generals, pressing straight to the rebel encampment, routed them utterly, beheaded Qun, and took more than two thousand heads and captives.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Shao then dispatched Yu, while Governor Hu Ping of Southern Qing Province sent his chief clerk Liu Renzhi; together they drove the generals straight against the enemy camp, inflicted a crushing defeat, killed Peng Qun, and took more than two thousand heads and prisoners.

sentences.zh: 肅宗嘉之，璽書勞問。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaoming commended this; an imperial sealed letter conveyed praise and inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaoming praised the victory and sent an imperial letter of commendation.

sentences.zh: 永安中，入為左將軍、給事黃門侍郎，又以前賞悆入徐之功未盡，增邑二百戶，進爵為侯。

translations.literal: In the Yong'an era he entered court as Left General and Governing Affairs Attendant of the Yellow Gate; moreover, because the earlier reward for Yu's achievement in entering Xu had not been fully given, his fief was increased by two hundred households and his nobility advanced to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yong'an era he was recalled as Left General and Attendant of the Yellow Gate. Because his reward for the Xu campaign had still not been fully granted, his fief was increased by two hundred households and he was raised to marquis.

sentences.zh: 雖任居通顯，志在謙退，迎送親賓，加於疇昔，而自無室宅，常假賃居止，布衣糲食，寒暑不變。

translations.literal: Although his office stood in open prominence, his will was humility and withdrawal; in receiving and sending off kin and guests he exceeded former times—yet he himself had no residence and always rented lodging; coarse cloth and plain food, unchanged in cold or heat.
translations.idiomatic: Though he held high office, he lived modestly, treating guests with even greater courtesy than before—yet he owned no house and always rented lodgings, dressing plainly and eating simply through every season.

sentences.zh: 莊帝嘉其清素，時復賜以錢帛。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhuang commended his purity and simplicity and from time to time again bestowed money and silk upon him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhuang admired his frugal integrity and occasionally sent him gifts of money and silk.

sentences.zh: 及東徐城民呂文欣殺刺史元大賓，南引賊眾，屯柵曲術，詔悆使持節、散騎常侍、安東將軍，為六州大使，與行臺樊子鵠討破之。

translations.literal: When the people of Dongxu City, Lü Wenxin, killed Governor Yuan Dabin and drew southern raiders southward, encamping at Qushu, an edict appointed Yu as Bearer of the Staff, Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, and Pacifying-the-East General, as envoy to six provinces; together with the Mobile Headquarters Fan Zihu he defeated and broke them.
translations.idiomatic: When Lü Wenxin of Dongxu City murdered Governor Yuan Dabin and summoned southern rebels to fortify Qushu, Lu Yu was commissioned as Bearer of the Staff, Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, and Pacifying-the-East General, envoy over six provinces; with Mobile Headquarters commander Fan Zihu he crushed the uprising.

sentences.zh: 文欣黨重以購之，文欣同逆人韓端正斬文欣送首，魁帥同死者十二人。

translations.literal: Wenxin's faction heavily offered bounty for him; Wenxin's fellow rebel Han Duanzheng beheaded Wenxin and sent the head; ringleaders and co-dying leaders numbered twelve men.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxin's followers placed a heavy price on Lu Yu's head, but Wenxin's own co-conspirator Han Duanzheng killed Wenxin and sent his head. Twelve rebel leaders died in the affair.

sentences.zh: 詔書褒慰。

translations.literal: An edict commended and comforted.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial edict praised and rewarded him.

sentences.zh: 還，拜鎮東將軍、金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Upon return he was appointed Pacifying-the-East General and Grand Master of the Golden Seal and Purple Girdle.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was appointed Pacifying-the-East General and Grand Master of the Golden Seal and Purple Girdle.

sentences.zh: 尋詔為使持節、兼尚書左僕射、東南道三徐行臺。

translations.literal: Soon he was edicted as Bearer of the Staff, Concurrent Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, and Mobile Headquarters for the Southeastern Route of the Three Xus.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed Bearer of the Staff, Concurrent Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, and mobile headquarters commander for the southeastern Three-Xu front.

sentences.zh: 至東郡，值尒朱仲遠陷西兗，向滑臺，詔與都督賀拔勝等拒仲遠。

translations.literal: Reaching Dong Commandery, he encountered Erzhu Zhongyuan's capture of Western Yanzhou and advance on Huaitai; an edict ordered him together with Area Commander Heba Sheng and others to resist Zhongyuan.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Dong Commandery, Erzhu Zhongyuan had overrun Western Yan Province and was marching on Huaitai; he was ordered to join Area Commander Heba Sheng and others in blocking Zhongyuan.

sentences.zh: 軍敗，還京。

translations.literal: The army was defeated; he returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The army was defeated, and he withdrew to the capital.

sentences.zh: 普泰中，加征東將軍，轉衞將軍、右光祿大夫、兼度支尚書、河北五州和糴大使。

translations.literal: During Putai, he was additionally appointed Eastern General; he was transferred to Guard General, Right Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, Concurrent Director of the Ministry of Revenue, and Commissioner for Harmonized Grain Purchases in the five provinces of Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: During the Putai era he was given the additional title of Eastern General, then made Guard General, Right Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, Concurrent Director of the Ministry of Revenue, and commissioner for harmonized grain purchases across the five Hebei provinces.

sentences.zh: 天平中，除梁州刺史。

translations.literal: During Tianping he was appointed Governor of Liang Province.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianping era he was appointed governor of Liang Province.

sentences.zh: 時滎陽民鄭榮業等聚眾反，圍逼州城。

translations.literal: At the time the commoners of Xingyang, Zheng Rongye and others, gathered crowds and rebelled, pressing and besieging the provincial capital.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Zheng Rongye and other men of Xingyang raised a rebel force and besieged the provincial seat.

sentences.zh: 悆不能固守，遂以城降。

translations.literal: Yu could not hold firm; thereupon he surrendered the city.
translations.idiomatic: Yu could not hold out and surrendered the city.

sentences.zh: 榮業送悆於關西。

translations.literal: Rongye sent Yu to Guanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Rongye sent Yu west of the pass into captivity.

sentences.zh: 張熠，[8]字景世，自云南陽西鄂人，漢侍中衡是其十世祖。

translations.literal: Zhang Yi, Editorial note marker [8] in the received text. style name Jingshi, claimed to be a native of Xi'e in Nanyang; Heng, Attendant-in-Ordinary of Han, was his tenth-generation ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yi, Footnote marker [8] in the received text. courtesy name Jingshi, claimed descent from Xi'e in Nanyang; his tenth-generation ancestor was Heng, Attendant-in-Ordinary of Han.

sentences.zh: 熠自奉朝請為揚州車騎府錄事參軍。

translations.literal: Yi rose from Court Gentleman for Imperial Audiences to Recorder in the Chariot-and-Cavalry Staff Office of Yang Province.
translations.idiomatic: From Court Gentleman for Imperial Audiences, Yi became recorder in the Yang Province Chariot-and-Cavalry staff office.

sentences.zh: 入除步兵校尉。

translations.literal: He entered [court service] and was appointed Commandant of Footsoldiers.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court service as Commandant of Footsoldiers.

sentences.zh: 永寧寺塔大興，[9]經營務廣，靈太后曾幸作所，凡有顧問，熠敷陳指畫，無所遺闕，太后善之。

translations.literal: The Yongning Temple pagoda was greatly constructed; Editorial note marker [9] in the received text. the project was vast in scope; Empress Dowager Ling once visited the construction site; whenever she had questions, Yi laid out and traced plans, omitting nothing; the empress dowager approved of him.
translations.idiomatic: When construction of the Yongning Temple pagoda was launched on a vast scale, Footnote marker [9] in the received text. Empress Dowager Ling visited the worksite; whenever she asked a question, Yi explained the design in full detail, and the empress dowager was pleased with him.

sentences.zh: 久之，除冠軍將軍、中散大夫。

translations.literal: After some time he was appointed Champion General and Gentleman Attendant at the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: After a time he was made Champion General and Gentleman Attendant at the Palace.

sentences.zh: 後為別將，隨長孫稚西征，轉平西將軍、太中大夫，為關西都督。

translations.literal: Later he served as a separate commander, following Zhangsun Zhi on the western campaign; he was transferred to Pacifying-the-West General and Grand Master for Persuasion, becoming Area Commander of Guanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as a detached commander under Zhangsun Zhi on the western campaign, then became Pacifying-the-West General and Grand Master for Persuasion, with command of Guanxi.

sentences.zh: 以功封長平縣開國男，食邑二百戶。

translations.literal: For merit he was enfeoffed as founding Baron of Changping County, with a fief of two hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: For his achievements he was enfeoffed as founding Baron of Changping County with a fief of two hundred households.

sentences.zh: 永安初，除平西將軍、岐州刺史、假安西將軍，尋加撫軍將軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongan he was appointed Pacifying-the-West General, Governor of Qi Province, and Acting Pacifying-the-West General; soon he was additionally made General Who Pacifies the Army.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Yongan era he was appointed Pacifying-the-West General and governor of Qi Province, with acting rank as Pacifying-the-West General; he was soon given the additional title of General Who Pacifies the Army.

sentences.zh: 矜恤貧弱，為民所愛。

translations.literal: He showed compassion to the poor and weak and was loved by the people.
translations.idiomatic: He cared for the poor and downtrodden and was beloved by the people.

sentences.zh: 代還，值元顥入洛，仍令復州，熠遂私還。

translations.literal: Upon replacement and return, he encountered Yuan Hao's entry into Luoyang; he was still ordered to resume his province, but Yi thereupon returned on his own.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended and he was replaced, Yuan Hao had entered Luoyang; though ordered to return to his post, Yi went home on his own instead.

sentences.zh: 莊帝還宮，出除鎮南將軍、東荊州刺史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuang returned to the palace, Yi was dismissed and appointed General Who Guards the South and Governor of Eastern Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Zhuang returned to the palace, Yi was made General Who Guards the South and governor of Eastern Jing Province.

sentences.zh: 尋加散騎常侍、征蠻大都督，轉荊州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he was additionally made Regular Attendant of the Scattered Riders and Grand Commander for the Punishment of the Barbarians, and transferred to Governor of Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon given the additional titles of Regular Attendant of the Scattered Riders and Grand Commander for the Punishment of the Barbarians, and transferred to governor of Jing Province.

sentences.zh: 值尒朱兆入洛，不行。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Zhao entered Luoyang, he did not go.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Zhao took Luoyang, he declined to take up the post.

sentences.zh: 普泰中，衞將軍、金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: During Putai, Guard General and Grand Master of the Golden Seal and Purple Girdle.
translations.idiomatic: During the Putai era he held the ranks of Guard General and Grand Master of the Golden Seal and Purple Girdle.

sentences.zh: 天平初，遷鄴草創，右僕射高隆之、吏部尚書元世儁奏曰：「南京宮殿，毀撤送都，連筏竟河，首尾大至，自非賢明一人，專委受納，則恐材木耗損，有闕經構。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianping, the capital was moved to Ye and was newly founded; Right Vice Director Gao Longzhi and Director of the Masters of Writing Yuan Shijun memorialized, saying: "The palaces of the Southern Capital are being dismantled and sent to the capital; rafts stretch along the river, the head and tail reach far; unless a single worthy and capable man is specially entrusted to receive and store them, we fear timber may be wasted and construction fall short.
translations.idiomatic: When Tianping began and Ye was chosen as the new capital, Right Vice Director Gao Longzhi and Director of the Masters of Writing Yuan Shijun memorialized: "The Southern Capital's palaces are being torn down and floated upriver to the new seat; the convoys stretch for miles. Unless one capable man is put in sole charge of receiving the timber, material will be wasted and construction delayed.

sentences.zh: 熠清貞素著，有稱一時，臣等輒舉為大將。

translations.literal: Yi is known for probity and has a reputation of the age; we your subjects venture to recommend him as Grand Commander.
translations.idiomatic: Yi is renowned for integrity and stands out among his contemporaries; we recommend him as chief construction officer.

sentences.zh: 」詔從之。

translations.literal: An edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 熠勤於其事。

translations.literal: Yi was diligent at his task.
translations.idiomatic: Yi applied himself diligently to the work.

sentences.zh: 尋轉營構左都將。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Left Chief General of Construction.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Left Chief General of Construction.

sentences.zh: 興和初，衞大將軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xinghe, Guard Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Xinghe era he was made Guard Grand General.

sentences.zh: 宮殿成，以本將軍除東徐州刺史。

translations.literal: When the palaces were completed, with his existing generalship he was appointed Governor of Eastern Xu Province.
translations.idiomatic: After the palaces were finished, he was appointed governor of Eastern Xu Province, retaining his general's rank.

sentences.zh: 三年，卒於州，時年六十。

translations.literal: In the third year he died in the province, at age sixty.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of his tenure he died in office, at the age of sixty.

sentences.zh: 贈驃騎大將軍、司空公、兗州刺史，諡曰懿。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given General of Agile Cavalry, Duke of Works, and Governor of Yan Province; his posthumous title was Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was made General of Agile Cavalry, Duke of Works, and governor of Yan Province, with the posthumous name Yi.

sentences.zh: 子孝直，武定末，司空騎兵參軍。

translations.literal: His son Xiaozhi, at the end of Wuding, was Cavalry Attendant to the Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xiaozhi, in the late Wuding era, served as Cavalry Attendant to the Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：成淹等身遭際會，俱得効其所能，以至於顯達，苟曰非才，亦何可以致。

translations.literal: The historian says: Cheng Yan and the others personally encountered the favorable moment, all obtaining to put forth their capacities, reaching to distinction and advancement; if one says they were not talented, how else could this be achieved.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: Cheng Yan and his fellows each met their moment and were able to put their talents to use, rising to prominence; had they lacked ability, how could they have attained such heights?

sentences.zh: 校勘記

translations.idiomatic: Collation Notes

sentences.zh: 何得以朱衣入山庭 通鑑卷一三七

translations.literal: "How can you enter the mourning hall in vermilion robes!" Zizhi tongjian juan 137
translations.idiomatic: On "How can you enter the mourning hall in vermilion robes!": Zizhi tongjian, juan 137

translations.literal: 〈page 4307〉

sentences.zh: 「山」作「凶」，當是。

translations.literal: "Mountain" is written as "mourning"; this is probably correct.
translations.idiomatic: "shan" (mountain/hall) should read "xiong" (mourning); this is the correct reading.

sentences.zh: 拜桃符征虜將軍豫州刺史 北史卷四六劉桃符傳「豫州」上有「東」字。

translations.literal: Appointment of Taofu as General Who Punishes the Barbarians and Governor of Yu Province: Bei Shi juan 46, Biography of Liu Taofu, before "Yu Province" has the character "East."
translations.idiomatic: On "appointed Taofu General Who Punishes the Barbarians and Governor of Yu Province": Bei Shi, juan 46 (Biography of Liu Taofu), has "East" before "Yu Province."

sentences.zh: 按上文稱東豫州刺史田益宗，桃符此授，即代益宗，當脫「東」字。

translations.literal: Note: above mentions Governor of Eastern Yu Province Tian Yizong; Taofu's appointment here replaces Yizong; "East" character is probably omitted.
translations.idiomatic: Note: the text above calls Tian Yizong Governor of Eastern Yu Province; Taofu's appointment here was to replace him—the character "East" has probably dropped out.

sentences.zh: 食邑二百戶 三朝本、汲本脫「百」字，北本、殿本「百」作「千」，南本、局本作「百」。

translations.literal: Fief of two hundred households: Sanchao and Ji editions omit "hundred"; Northern and Dian editions read "hundred" as "thousand"; Southern and Bureau editions have "hundred."
translations.idiomatic: On "fief of two hundred households": the Sanchao and Ji editions omit "hundred"; the Northern and Dian editions read "hundred" as "thousand"; the Southern and Bureau editions read "hundred."

sentences.zh: 按下張熠傳稱「封長平縣開國男，食邑二百戶」，同一等級，封戶雖或有多少，不會相去懸殊，今從南、局本。

translations.literal: Note: below, Zhang Yi's biography reads "Enfeoffed as founding Baron of Changping County, fief of two hundred households"; same rank—though fief households may vary somewhat, they would not differ greatly; now follow Southern and Bureau editions.
translations.idiomatic: Note: the biography of Zhang Yi below gives "Enfeoffed as founding Baron of Changping County, fief of two hundred households" for the same rank; fief sizes may differ, but not wildly—Southern and Bureau editions are followed here.

sentences.zh: 元興世寒因元叉之勢託其交道相用為州主簿 按上文不云元興曾官州主簿，託附元叉時，他已由司徒記室參軍遷尚書殿中郎，領中書舍人，不得方因叉勢為州主簿。

translations.literal: Yuanxing's family was poor; relying on Yuan Cha's power, using their connection, Xiang was employed as provincial chief clerk: Note: above does not say Yuanxing ever served as provincial chief clerk; when he used Yuan Cha's influence, he had already moved from Recorder in the Minister of Works' staff to Palace Attendant in the Masters of Writing, concurrently Palace Secretariat Attendant—he could not at that time have become provincial chief clerk through Cha's influence.
translations.idiomatic: On "Yuanxing's family was poor; through Yuan Cha's power he used their connection to have Xiang appointed provincial chief clerk": the text above never says Yuanxing held that office; by the time he relied on Cha's influence he had already risen from Recorder in the Minister of Works' staff to Palace Attendant in the Masters of Writing and concurrent Palace Secretariat Attendant—he could hardly then have used Cha's favor to become provincial chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 疑上脫子某，託元叉之勢官州主簿的是元興之子。

translations.literal: Suspect the text above omits "son so-and-so"; it was Yuanxing's son who, through Yuan Cha's influence, served as provincial chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Probably a name such as "his son ___" has dropped out above; it was Yuanxing's son, not Yuanxing himself, who held the provincial chief clerkship through Yuan Cha's influence.

translations.idiomatic: Fang Xu of East Qinghe rebelled: juan 21, part 2 (Biography of Prince of Pengcheng Shao), Cefu juan 121

translations.idiomatic: reads "Xu" as "Qing"; Zizhi tongjian, juan 151

translations.literal: reads "Xiang."
translations.idiomatic: which reads "Xiang."

sentences.zh: 參卷九校記。

translations.literal: See collation note in juan 9.
translations.idiomatic: See the collation note in juan 9.

sentences.zh: 師次鄖城 按鄖城遠在今湖北安陸，琅邪一帶不聞有此城名，「鄖」字疑訛。

translations.literal: The army halted at Yuncheng: Note: Yuncheng is far away in present-day Anlu, Hubei; the Langye region has never been heard to have this place name; the character "Yun" is suspected corrupt.
translations.idiomatic: On "the army halted at Yuncheng": Yuncheng lies far to the south in present-day Anlu, Hubei; no such place is known in the Langye region—the character "Yun" is probably corrupt.

sentences.zh: 張熠 北史卷四六「熠」作「燿」。

translations.literal: Zhang Yi: Bei Shi juan 46 reads "Yi" as "Yao."
translations.idiomatic: On "Zhang Yi": Bei Shi, juan 46, reads "Yao" for "Yi."

sentences.zh: 永寧寺塔大興 諸本「永寧」下有「中」字。

translations.literal: Yongning Temple pagoda greatly constructed: in various editions after "Yongning" there is the character "middle."
translations.idiomatic: On "construction of the Yongning Temple pagoda was launched": various editions insert "zhong" (middle/period) after "Yongning."

sentences.zh: 按魏無「永寧」年號。

translations.literal: Note: Wei has no reign era "Yongning."
translations.idiomatic: Note: the Northern Wei had no reign era called Yongning.

sentences.zh: 永寧是寺名，屢見本書，「中」字衍，今刪。

translations.literal: Yongning is a temple name, frequently seen in this book; the character "middle" is superfluous; deleted here.
translations.idiomatic: Yongning is a temple name, common in this history; "zhong" is a spurious addition and is omitted here.
